text: Keeping low to the ground will also help you\nmaintain your aim.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: You got all that?\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: In this mission, you're prohibited from killing any\nenemy combatants.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: And if you're spotted even once, you fail.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: Bottom line: proceed with caution.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: Stay low to the ground. If there are any enemies\nnearby,\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: walk slowly and don't make a sound…\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: Another good technique is to hide behind\nsomething\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: and do <I=ESEARCH> to check out your enemies.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: And then there's always the classic trick of\nthrowing\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: an empty ammo magazine to distract the enemy.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: Use your ears as well as your eyes.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: The Surround Indicator is a handy way to "see"\nsounds as visual data.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: So all I have to do here is shoot down the Fulton\nrecovery balloons, right?\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: Right. And don't shoot the soldier dangling\nunderneath by mistake.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: I'd go with the sniper rifle,\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: but really, any weapon will work as long as you aim\ncarefully.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Balloon popping... heh.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: You might get more balloons if you do this one as\na CO-OPS.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: The, uh... ha, ha... sky's the limit!\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: Look at it this way\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: - it'd get real depressing real quick if every single\nmission were a bloodbath.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: It's good to have a nice, relaxing challenge like this\nonce in a while, you know?\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: And c'mon, don't those Fulton balloons look tasty?\nLike big, juicy, floating pigs...\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: ...Yeah, sure, whatever. So this is called a "Pooyan\nmission."\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: What's that supposed to mean?\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: When I was a kid, my neighbors had a pet pig they\ncalled Pooyan.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: Every time I see a Fulton balloon, it reminds me of\nthat litle porker.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: OK, but the objective here is to pop those\nballoons, right?\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Doesn't sound like a good idea getting emotionally\nattached...\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: Good point. Man, if only those were real pigs\ndangling from the balloons...\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: Now wouldn't that be something...\n
Enemies that steal your items will try and escape\nthe area.\n
Make it a priority to take them out first.\n
Don't let them make off with your stuff.\n
We're seeing multiple hostiles in this area.\n
It's not going to be easy going it alone.\n
I'd recommend taking this one on as a two-man cell\nin CO-OPS.\n
Alternatively, you could try planting Claymores\nalong the routes they walk.\n
We need you to stop that nuke, Boss.\n
We'll keep you safe, no matter what it takes!\n
It's going to take more than small arms fire to take\ndown a truck.\n
Some kind of rocket's your best bet.\n
Another tactic to try would be setting off an\nexplosion from afar.\n
You could also call in a support strike,\n
if you can manage to tag them with a marker...\n
It'll take more than one missile to sink Mother\nBase, but if we do get hit,\n
we'll obviously need time, manpower, and materials\nto repair the damage.\n
Do everything you can to keep Mother Base safe.\n
And, ah, at the risk of stating the obvious: if a\nmissile hits you,\n
you're toast. So don't get hit.\n
You'll be using C4 for demolition.\n
As you might imagine, it's gonna make a big noise\nwhen it detonates.\n
For your own safety, make sure you put plenty of\ndistance\n
between yourself and the C4 before detonating it.\n
Boss, we're not sure where your gear is being\nstored.\n
Amanda and her crew tell me they've managed to\nidentify several different categories\n
of mercenaries employed by the CIA.\n
Give me a rundown. Sounds like info I could use.\n
No problem. I'll go through them in order.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: The type of enemy you'll be seeing most\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: is the type that patrols and guards a specific\noperational area.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: For the sake of convenience, Amanda's crew calls\nthe outdoor ones "patrolmen,"\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: and the indoor ones "guards."\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: They might look like they're just out for a stroll,\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: but don't be fooled - they're sharper than they\nlook.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: All of their senses are finely honed.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: Normally they'll patrol along fixed routes,\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: but when the alert level is raised they'll assume a\nmore efficient alert posture\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: and focus on defending specific points. That's bad\nfor you.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: Obviously they can hold their own in combat,\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: and with body armor it'll be even harder to take\nthem down.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: If they're wearing a bulletproof helmet,\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: you can forget about one-shot kills. Just a heads\nup.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: You'll need to be smart about using camo and pick\nyour routes.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: The most important thing is to avoid detection.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: When the enemy spots you and goes on alert, they\nmay call in a backup strike team.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: These assault teams are heavily armed, well\ntrained, and highly dangerous.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: Amanda's crew calls them "commandos."\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: Unlike the patrolmen, these guys will actively,\nrelentlessly track and hunt you down - like hounds.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Hounds to hunt a former FOXHOUND... Bring it on.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: They won't give up easily even if they lose sight of\nyou.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: They'll clear out any likely hiding places they come\nacross.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: So don't get too comfy in one spot or you might\nget caught again.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: Keep your eyes fixed on them and what they're\ndoing.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: Also, be aware that commando gear includes body\narmor.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: So don't think you can deal with them by going in\nguns blazing.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: All I've got to do is find an exposed weak point\nand...\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: Exactly.\n
There's one type of commando you really need to\nwatch out for,\n
and that's the kind toting shotguns.\n
They can take a few hits and still keep charging\nyou.\n
And believe me, you don't want them closing in\nbetween those shotgun blasts.\n
When they start charging, you need to stop them\nimmediately.\n
Use something with serious stopping power.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: We've also confirmed that some of the enemies\nspecialize in ambushes.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: Amanda's crew calls them "scouts."\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: They'll blend themselves in with the terrain and the\nvegetation.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: Then, when they see you, they'll swoop in.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: They fight pretty much like commandos\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: and will use clearing techniques to flush you out.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: In addition to wielding normal weapons, the scouts\nalso carry wires.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Hm... Sounds like these guys know their CQC.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: Could be. We've been getting reports of CQC\nattacks being blocked by wires.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: Stay alert.\n
Scouts are outfitted with camouflage to help them\nhide.\n
Some of them look kind of weird, like they've got\nseaweed growing all over them.\n
Ah, ghillie suits.\n
Not much difference between them and any other\nscout in terms of combat ability,\n
but it does make them harder to spot.\n
I'm sure it does.\n
You've come across these before?\n
Yeah. The Soviet Union...\n
The first time, it took me a full hour to find the\nguy and take him out...\n
Kaz, do you know if they shine?\n
...Shine. Like how?\n
Like from their heads.\n
Their heads?\n
How about their hair? Do they have a lot of it?\n
What are you talking about? How the hell would I\nknow?\n
How about a parrot? Did anybody hear a parrot\nsquawk?\n
A parrot? Look, Snake, you're talking to the wrong\nguy.\n
I mean, Cecile's the bird expert...\n
Wait a second, what am I saying? You're not\nmaking any sense to begin with!\n
Never mind. It's... a long story. I'll figure out another\nway. Forget about it.\n
Yeah, I'll do that.\n
Anyway, we've already lost too many good people\nto these surprise encounters.\n
Make sure you don't end up like one of them.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: There are areas out there where enemy soldiers\nare\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: deployed in multiple layers for extra coverage.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: More than a few of those will be attacking you\nfrom a distance\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: - rooftops and far-off vantage points.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: Try not to get too distracted by nearby enemies,\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: because you could be leaving yourself wide open\nto longer-range attacks.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: I'll be careful.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: Enemy tanks, armored vehicles,\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: and attack choppers are always accompanied by a\ncombat squad.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: The soldiers aren't particularly tough on their own.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: What makes them formidable is how well they work\ntogether as a team.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: As if you didn't have enough to worry about with\nthe machine.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Good. I like a challenge.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: Yeah, well, see how you feel when you actually\nhave to face them in battle.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: Snake, whatever you do, don't let them surround\nyou.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: The last thing you need is to get pushed into the\nvehicle's kill zone.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: And pay attention to what your enemies say to\neach other.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: You can improve your chances by figuring out\nwhat they're planning\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: and using it to preempt their movements.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: You don't always have to go toe to toe to win a\nfight.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: Think like a guerrilla.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Got it.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: Enemies carrying shields can be a real pain in the\nass.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: To hear Amanda tell it, trying to fight those\nbastards\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: while they sit behind their shields taking pistol\nshots at you\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: is enough to make you want to rip your hair out.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: Get around and flank them if you can.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: You might want to try blinding them with smoke or\nstun grenades first.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: Also, armor-piercing rounds should make it a little\neasier to punch through their shields.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: Use 'em if you've got 'em.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: We know there are variations in the kinds of gear\npatrolmen and commandos wear,\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: especially the body armor.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: Our scouts report that an enemy's defense and\nfiring accuracy\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: are directly proportional to how heavy their gear is.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Those must be the guys with the highest combat\nskills.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: They can fight in heavier gear without their\nperformance suffering.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: Supposedly it's pretty easy to tell the difference in\ngear just by looking.\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: So remember:\n

speaker: 0x0e463a34
text: use extra caution when dealing with enemies\nwearing heavy gear.\n
Enemies will try to fight you from different\ndistances\n
based on the weapon they've got equipped.\n
When you meet an enemy, get a good look at what\nthey're carrying\n
- it can make or break your chances in battle.\n
Enemies carrying handguns and shotguns will try\nand get in close.\n
That makes them dangerous, but at the same time\neasier to hit.\n
Keep you wits about you and you can turn a threat\ninto an opportunity.\n
Enemies carrying assault rifles and machine guns\n
will usually fire at you from farther away.\n
Use whatever cover you can find,\n
then return fire with a few well-placed shots of\nyour own.\n
Don't expect enemies carrying sniper rifles\n
or rocket launchers to get up close and personal.\n
They'll be constantly moving from place to place\n
looking for an opening to snipe at you. Tricky\nbastards.\n
Eye for an eye, tooth for a tooth, - go with the\nsniper rifle.\n
Make sure you stay out of their line of sight,\n
and when they expose themselves, take 'em down!\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: Costa Rica means "rich coast" in Spanish.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Is it true that Columbus was the one who came up\nwith the name?\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: Your guess is as good as mine. But it is true\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: that Columbus landed his ships near Limón back in\nthe Age of Exploration.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: He wrote in his diary that when he landed,\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: the indígena showered him with gifts of gold.\nHence the name.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: It sounds a little strange to me.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: There is no way they could find that much gold in\nCosta Rica.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Columbus originally set sail in search of the\nlegendary land of gold.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Maybe he was just nuts about the stuff.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: Costa Rica is rich enough without it.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: Look at the forests and the animals, and the\npeace-loving people...\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: That is what I want to protect.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: ...I know how you feel.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: Democracy took root in Costa Rica before\nanywhere else in Central America.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: Sure, we had coups and dictators and all, but\nnever a total meltdown.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: That is, until 26 years ago...\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: The civil war. Yeah, I understand you lost your\ngrandparents.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: It started with a dispute over alleged fraud in the\npresidential election.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: What I don't understand is why friend turned\nagainst friend\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: when they could have talked it out instead.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Yeah, that... would have been nice.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: Even today, some buildings still have bullet holes\nfrom the civil war.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: A quarter century later, and it is a tragedy we\nticos cannot forget... Must not forget.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: It was the year after the civil war that the army\nwas constitutionally abolished.\n
A new president was elected this year - President\nOduber.\n
He seems to be distancing himself from the United\nStates.\n
He's limited the privileges granted to American\nbanks, lifted the sanctions on Cuba...\n
Our last president was so pro-U.S., people\nsuspected he was in bed with the CIA.\n
You think the CIA's doing this because it feels\nthreatened by the president's shift in policy...?\n
It is possible. But would they really bring in such a\nhuge army just because of that?\n
Part of our job is finding out.\n
Exactly. Thanks, Snake. Peace.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: So are you a student at the University for Peace,\nPaz?\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: No, I am still in high school.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: But Professor Gálvez lets me visit his office and\nstudy with him every now and then.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: International law, security, conflict resolution,\nhuman rights...\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: We study all these subjects and then use them to\nbuild the foundations of peace.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Yeah, I get it... I'd just never heard the UN had a\nUniversity for Peace before.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: Oh, that. Well, to be precise, it is still being set up.\nThey have started conducting research, but\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: the UN has not passed the necessary resolution\nyet.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: Professor Gálvez couldn't wait that long...\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Oh, uh, right.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: Costa Rica abolished its army,\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: and has also hosted the Central American Court of\nJustice.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: It is the perfect place to build a university like\nours, don't you think?\n
Professor Gálvez was a KGB spy...?\n
I thought he helped me out of genuine concern for\nCosta Rica's future...\n
You didn't know?\n
How could I?! Believe me, Snake.\n
He introduced himself as a peace researcher at\nthe university.\n
He had an office and credentials and everything...\n
They're masters at creating cover personas. They\nthink of everything\n
- ID papers, jobs, sometimes even families.\n
Don't feel bad you didn't see through it.\n
But you did?\n
From the first time we met.\n
I wish you'd told me...\n
Sorry. I didn't know if it'd be right.\n
You might have gotten mixed up in things you\nshouldn't.\n
That is impressive, though. Sizing him up him at a\nsingle glance.\n
He reeked.\n
Reeked?\n
He had this unmistakable air about him...\n
The air of someone who's been given a mission\nand will see it through no matter what.\n
Like me. I could just smell it.\n
That is amazing, Snake!\n
Nah, I'm just kidding. It was his prosthetic hand.\n
Why would a professor from a peace university\nneed a tool for assassination?\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: That coffee you guys brought us is pretty damn\ngood.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: Isn't it? Costa Rican coffee is the best.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: The Central Basin has all the right conditions for\ngrowing coffee.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: It is high in elevation, with steady temperatures\nand well-drained, volcanic soils.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: The "professor" certainly seems attached to it.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: The coffee we drank on the boat coming over was\nawful. It put him in such a terrible mood.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: How come I never hear about Costa Rican coffee,\nthen?\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: Because it gets bought up by wholesalers and\nmixed with beans from other countries...\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: It is really a shame. Such wonderful beans and\nnobody knows they're from Costa Rica.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: They should launch an ad campaign or something.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: Right! I hope one day people will recognize Costa\nRican coffee for what it is.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: I'm with you there.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Are there any large-scale ruins in Costa Rica, Paz?\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: There's a place east of Cartago called Guayabo.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: They have ruins there, but they're not especially\nbig.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Not the place I'm thinking of... Any others?\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: Well, if you go a little way across the border into\nNicaragua,\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: there's a place called La Fortaleza de la\nInmaculada Concepción. That's the only famous one.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Then what were those ruins I saw from up on\nIrazu...?\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: There are a lot of things we still do not know\nabout Costa Rica's ancient civilizations.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: There are giant stone spheres throughout the\ncountry.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: What they were used for is still a mystery.\n
Paz, you said Costa Rica has no army, right?\n
Correct. Article 12 of the constitution declared\n
that the army as a permanent institution is\nabolished.\n
It does permit us to organize armed forces for\nnational defense\n
based on inter-American treaties.\n
Only temporarily, then.\n
In effect, yes. But in the years since the\nconstitution took effect,\n
Costa Rica has not once raised an army.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Paz. How does your country defend itself without\nan army?\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Especially in a rough neighborhood like Central\nAmerica.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: With the right kind of diplomacy.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: If we live up to our ideals and earn the respect of\nother countries,\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: the international community will support us.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: The two times Nicaragua actually did invade,\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: the conflict was resolved diplomatically under OAS\n(Organization of American States) auspices.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Doesn't that leave you depending on the U.S. after\nall?\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: American influence is unmatched, it is true.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: San Jose was critical of American policy at the\ntime...\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: But America supported us all the same. It was\nbecause we practiced peaceful diplomacy...\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: That is what I like to think.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: That's one way to approach it, sure.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: But there are countries out there who'll use force\nno matter how bad it looks.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: Maybe so... I know my way of thinking probably\nlooks naïve to you.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: But it's not like we expect peace without working\nfor it.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: Diplomacy is a battle in itself.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: And we have to make the effort\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: to seek out causes of misfortune and nip them in\nthe bud.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: It was that kind of thinking that got me trapped in\ntheir base...\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: I'm not blaming you. You haven't done anything\nwrong.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: The army was abolished 25 years ago, the year\nafter the civil war.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: I learned about the sorrow of civil war from a very\nyoung age.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: The futility of countrymen fighting each other, and\nthe tragedy...\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: Costa Rica learned the hard way. That is why it\nabolished its army.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: It decided to pour its efforts into education\ninstead.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: More teachers than soldiers was the slogan.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Education is essential, no question.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Even Che used to teach reading and writing in\nbetween guerrilla campaigns.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: Costa Rica was poor at the time. We didn't have\nmany resources.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: I suppose we had to pick one or the other - the\nmilitary or the schools.\n
Kaz was telling me Japan has a peace constitution,\ntoo.\n
That is right. Apparently when Costa Rica was\ndrafting its constitution,\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Sadly ironic, given who's occupying it now.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: That war was the reason Costa Rica abolished the\narmy.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: Please, Snake! Get them out of our country!\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: I intend to.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Paz, what was the government thinking building a\npower plant at the top of a mountain?\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: With no river to replenish the water, the lake would\ndry up pretty quick...\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: ...If it were an ordinary power plant. But the plan\ncalled for a pumped storage power plant.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Pumped storage power plant? Kaz mentioned that,\ntoo. What is that?\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: It's a facility that generates electricity by pumping\nwater up to the lake,\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: then letting it run back down.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Seems Sisyphean to me.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: If they turned the water into electricity as soon as\nthey'd pumped it up, sure.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: But a pumped storage plant acts as a kind of\nbattery.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: A battery?\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: For instance, they could pump at night,\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: when there's surplus electricity, and store it for\nlater use.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: If they need extra power during the day,\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: they can generate it using water pumped up during\nthe night.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: I get it. It's a little more difficult to adjust output\nwith thermal or nuclear plants.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: The thing is, Costa Rica won't have enough\nelectricity to meet its needs.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: Right now - there is no surplus.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Maybe that's what put the brakes on the project.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Must've played right into the CIA's hands.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: This area is a tropical cloud forest, continually\ncovered in a thick mist.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: It is quite a mystical place.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Selba de la Leche... "Forest of Milk." I can barely\nsee in front of me.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: There you go again. The forest is basically sitting\nin a cloud,\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: so of course it's going to be hard to see.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: But you know, the cloud forest is the only place\nmany exotic creatures can live.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Well, if they're not edible, I'm not interested.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: Snake! I'll have you know people travel from all\naround the world\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: to witness Costa Rica's unique fauna!\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: Snake, watch out for the frogs.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Why, they bite? Relax, no frog's ever eaten a snake.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Although I've feasted on a few frogs' legs myself...\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: But, they're dangerous! They're poisonous!\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Poisonous?\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: Poison dart frogs live up to their name, I assure\nyou.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: Their poison is so strong the indígena use them to\nmake poison-tipped arrows.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: Some secrete poison through their skin - even\ntouching them can be dangerous.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: So don't go petting them or anything.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: So... I can't eat one?\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: I'm warning you!\n
Catarata de la Muerte means "Waterfall of Death."\n
How cheerful.\n
I am sure it will be no problem for you, Snake,\n
especially compared to all the dire situations\nyou've faced in the past.\n
Easy to say now. We'll see what really happens.\n
Sorry. Still, you have surprised me. Everything they\nsay about the legend is true.\n
I'm neither hero nor legend. But for some reason, I\ndon't mind you calling me that.\n
Thanks. Be careful, Snake. Peace!\n
Selba de la Muerte, huh?\n
Forest of Death. Wouldn't want to get lost here.\n
Sure wouldn't. But do not worry, I will be your guide.\n
Happy to hear it.\n
By the way, Snake, you know much about sloths?\n
Just the name.\n
They are amazing. Sloths spend almost all their\nlives up in trees,\n
except for when they have to go to the bathroom.\nPlus, they barely eat a thing.\n
What? How do they survive?\n
Why do you think they're called "sloths"?\n
They hardly move, so they hardly burn any energy.\n
They're also able to maintain a low body\ntemperature, lowering their metabolism further,\n
and allowing them to survive on very little.\n
Wouldn't that make it easier for them to be picked\noff by predators?\n
They stick to the trees, helping them blend in and\nstay out of sight.\n
They say there are even some sloths that grow\nmoss when they reach a certain age.\n
Like some sort of fairy tale forest hermit, huh?\n
I knew a great old sniper once.\n
Guess he was even more in tune with nature than I\nthought.\n
Old sniper? What are you talking about?\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: La Ruinas de Xochiquetzal will be around there.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: They have not been restored at all, so they may\nwell be covered in plants.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Xochiquetzal?\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: An Aztec goddess of fertility and beauty.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: They say she was always accompanied by birds\nand butterflies.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: One theory states she was the mother of the god\nknown as Quetzalcoatl.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Quetzalcoatl...\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: The quetzal is said to be an incarnation of\nQuetzalcoatl, hence its name.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: I get it. Well, this place definitely matches the\natmosphere of a cloud forest.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: Now, it may have seen better days, but that is still\na temple.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: So, be sure to show respect when you're inside.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: If the mood strikes me.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: Hmph! Well, you've got no one to blame but yourself\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: if Xochiquetzal strikes you down.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: I do not know if I recall such large ruins being\nthere...\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Well, didn't you say there's a lot we don't know\nabout Costa Rica's ancient civilizations?\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: You talked about some giant stone balls, too. What\nare those?\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: Oh, the Stone Spheres of Costa Rica?\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: They're an assortment of giant spheres carved\nfrom stone\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: that were discovered in the jungles of Costa Rica\nabout 50 years ago.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: What's so special about that?\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: What if I told you some of them are nearly perfect\nspheres?\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: And that they were carved out of granite, which is\nquite a hard substance.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Hmm, could be good for laying a trap.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: And if they're spherical, they'd roll easily, too...\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: Snake...\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: So tell me, what do they mine around here?\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: Gold, if I am not mistaken.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Gold?! No kidding. I wonder what'd be the fastest\nway to...\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: I do not know how much success they've had.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: You do not hear of anyone still operating mines\naround here.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Oh...\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: Generally speaking, people here are not too thrilled\nwith outside capital\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: coming in and taking away the country's natural\nresources.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: Four years ago, a group of protestors hurled\nstones at the parliament building\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: when people found out the country had been\nbestowing mining rights to foreign companies.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: They must have had to clear a considerable\namount of forest to open up that mine.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: No doubt. So much for any hiding places, too.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: And it is not just the forest. Without the proper\nprecautions,\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: the mine's waste water could pollute the\ngroundwater.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: And to top it all off, they're developing nuclear\nweapons there, too.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: How can people care so little about their own\ncountry?\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: ...I'm not the one to ask about that.\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: Well, you may have abandoned your country,\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: but you still treasure where you came from.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: You think so?\n

speaker: 0x0e55d959
text: Sure. I know you do.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Paz, you... I... Whatever you do, never stop loving\nyour country.\n
Since it was founded, my country has not once\nbeen able to choose its own path.\n
First Spain, then America. Over one hundred years\nof this...\n
I know.\n
In the 19th century,\n
an American mercenary named William Walker\nseized power in Nicaragua.\n
I'd heard he exploited rivalries between the political\nparties.\n
Even after we expelled him,\n
the Americans sent in their Marines under the\npretext of quelling political unrest.\n
And the real reason?\n
To intimidate the government and thwart the\nconstruction of the Nicaragua Canal.\n
I thought the U.S. already has the rights to build a\ncanal in Nicaragua...\n
They never intended to build a canal there. They\nhad already started digging in Panama.\n
A canal in Nicaragua would break up the Panama\nCanal's monopoly,\n
reason enough for America to stick its nose into\nour affairs.\n
They snagged the rights so nobody else could\nbuild there...\n
It was General Sandino who finally stood up to los\nyanquis.\n
General Sandino waged a guerrilla war against the\nMarines,\n
at last driving them out. He was a true hero, and -\nto us Sandinistas - like a father.\n
But when they pulled out, the Americans left us\nsomething to remember them by.\n
The National Guard.\n
Yes, la Guardia. In name, a peacekeeping force.\n
But in reality, Commander Somoza's personal army,\nanswering to no one else.\n
Unable to stay silent, General Sandino went to\nprotest...\n
and was assassinated by Somoza as he made his\nway home.\n
It was then that Somoza and los sapos\n
began to eat our country alive, from the inside.\n
It has been 40 years since the Somoza family\nbecame the rulers of Nicaragua.\n
With la Guardia at their command, no one can\nchallenge them.\n
You came here on the run from the National\nGuard, right?\n
Si. They took everything. Our land, our homes, our\njobs...\n
Now belong to Somoza.\n
Si. The law, too. He's even got the judges in his\npocket. You defy him, you face death.\n
Everyone bows and scrapes before la Guardia.\n
Even then, you might get a beating if they are in a\nbad mood.\n
And you're trying to change things.\n
That's not all. The Somozas have used their power\nto line their pockets.\n
They confiscate people's land and hand it to\nmembers of the Somoza family.\n
By now, close to half the farmland in Nicaragua is\ntheirs.\n
We were powerless. Until...\n
You remember the earthquake two years ago?\n
Yeah. I heard it the capital was hit pretty hard.\n
We lost Managua, our capital city.\n
People sent aid from all around the world. Tears of\nsorrow turned to tears of joy.\n
Yet almost all of it was embezzled by the Somozas.\n
They sold out those who'd lost everything - for\nmoney! They feasted on our country's suffering!\n
Public resentment is at the boiling point.\n
The Somozas' days are numbered. We will see to it.\n
The first Somoza was originally no more than the\ncommander of la Guardia.\n
Ordinarily, a man of his station could never hope to\nbecome president.\n
But the president at the time had no power to\nback him.\n
The only one with the strength to oppose him was\nGeneral Sandino.\n
....No. Better to say the General was the only one\nwho dared oppose him.\n
There was nothing special about him.\n
Above all, it takes a strong will to see justice done.\nThat is what he taught us.\n
It's also what motivated Somoza to have him killed...\n
Yes. The rest was easy. He got rid of the\npresident, taking office in a sham election.\n
And once he had power, he never gave it up.\n
Talk about heavy-handed.\n
He had the Americans backing him, that's why.\n
They didn't want to hand over power to a\nrebellious general.\n
Even so, it's hard to believe Washington would give\nits blessing to a guy like that.\n
The American President at the time put it this way:\n
Somoza may be a son of a bitch, but he's our son\nof a bitch.\n
In other words, better a dog or los sapos (Somoza\nand counter-revolutionaries)\n
than an anti-US regime.\n
The Managua Earthquake struck two years ago,\nthe day before Christmas Eve.\n
Giant cracks opened up in the streets.\n
Sleeping children were crushed in collapsing\nhouses.\n
No chance to escape. No visit from Santa Claus.\n
Thanks to Somoza, the old houses could not even\nget rebuilt... It was a nightmare.\n
I heard the epicenter was right in the middle of the\ncity.\n
Even today, it's too dangerous to build on top of\nthe fault line.\n
The city center is still in ruins.\n
And to make things worse, Somoza stole the\nrecovery money.\n
We must not fail. We owe it to those who lost their\nlives.\n
We will defeat Somoza.\n
The river that flows between Nicaragua and Costa\nRica is el Río San Juan.\n
It connects Lago Cocibolca to el Mar Caribe.\n
It is a gentle river, safe even for small boats. You\nhave to watch out for the sharks, though.\n
Sharks? In a river?\n
El tiburón toro live in the river. But there's nothing\nto fear. San Juan will protect you always.\n
Juan?\n
The Rio San Juan takes its name from San Juan,\nthe man who baptized Jesús.\n
The man you call John the Baptist in your country.\n
John, huh... I'll be careful anyway. I'd hate to drown\n- end up a John Doe.\n
There is a volcanic island in Lago Cocibolca called\nOmetepe.\n
It's formed from two connected volcanoes, shaped\nlike a porongo (gourd).\n
The one with smoke coming out of it?\n
That's the one. The smoking volcano is\nConcepción. It erupts once in a while.\n
The other one is Maderas.\n
It's never erupted in recorded history. There's a\nlake in the caldera at the top.\n
A crater lake... Let's hope there's not another\nunderground factory inside...\n
Don't say that!\n
If Peace Walker's nukes detonated there, it would\ndestabilize the magma underneath.\n
It could cause the volcano to erupt again.\n
If that happens, my country is doomed. Snake, you\nmust stop Peace Walker!\n
We are Sandinistas, the heirs of General Sandino's\nwill.\n
Sandino... the father of modern guerrilla warfare.\n
To you, maybe. To us, he's more like a real father.\n
That why you named yourselves after him?\n
Of course. La Frente Sandinista de Liberación\nNacional...\n
the Sandinista National Liberation Front is named\nin his honor.\n
We share the General's goal - to take back our\ncountry's freedom.\n
In his day, from America. In ours, from the despot\nSomoza.\n
Times have changed, but the song remains the\nsame.\n
Patria Libre o Morir... That is our slogan.\n
El Che used to say the same thing, you know?\n
Patria o Muerte... the slogan of the Cuban\nRevolution.\n
So you're fighting for a socialist revolution, too,\nthen?\n
No. It's not about ideology. We only want to live\nnormal lives.\n
We are sick of living in a country where you can\nbe beaten for walking down the street.\n
Where you never know if your neighbor is snitching\non you.\n
Our goal is to give back the country to its people.\n
Yeah. The Cuban Revolution started out like that,\ntoo...\n
We are few in number, but we will win.\n
Victoria o muerte. For a revolutionary, there is no\nother fate.\n
Augusto César Sandino... general and hero of\nNicaragua.\n
Fifty years ago, conflict broke out between the\npolitical parties of Nicaragua.\n
The U.S. Marines intervened in the name of\nrestoring order.\n
The only one who refused to listen to their call for\nreconciliation was General Sandino.\n
One man against the Marines... That takes guts.\n
The General wasn't a professional soldier. Neither\nwere his compadres.\n
And they certainly could not match the Marines'\nequipment.\n
But he used the land to his advantage, lurking in\nthe fields and hills of Nicaragua,\n
and using surprise attacks to harass the Marines.\n
I know. I've read plenty of textbooks on guerrilla\nwarfare.\n
In the end, he drove them out. He was truly a role\nmodel for us.\n
Yeah, but that was the '30s - didn't the Depression\nhave something to do with it?\n
It takes cash to wage war.\n
Perhaps. But there is no denying what the General\naccomplished.\n
The people hailed him as the "General de Hombres\nLibres" - the general of free men.\n
They loved him. And then...\n
He was assassinated - by Anastasio Somoza\nGarcia, commander of la Guardia.\n
The father of the current Somoza.\n
Somoza had the Americans' backing. That is the\nway things were.\n
The General may be dead, and the times may have\nchanged,\n
but his will lives on inside each of us.\n
We are the sons and daughters of General Sandino.\n
Hey. How's the watermelon business these days?\n
Not bad. I hear the compas back home are hanging\nin there, too.\n
Good to hear.\n
...You know our nickname. I'm impressed.\n
No wonder they call you Boss.\n
You used to hide your weapons in hollowed-out\nwatermelons,\n
smuggle 'em right past the National Guard.\n
You even transported pineapple grenades that\nway.\n
The name caught on among sympathizers in the\nregion and...\n
What are you talking about?\n
Huh?\n
They call us watermelon sellers because the\nGeneral's name\n
sounds like the word for watermelon, sandía.\n
...Really?\n
Si.\n
Dammit, Kaz...\n
A revolution to bring peace to your country, huh.\n
No matter how much we fight, peace never gets\nany closer, does it?\n
I do not like it, but it is the only way.\n
If we do not fight back, they'll just keep exploiting\nus.\n
You want proof? Look at our country's history.\n
Revolution is a means and not an end, I know.\n
When the revolution is victorious, I want my\ncountry to be at peace.\n
But to bring peace, we have to first eliminate that\ntraitorous scum.\n
It's an old saying: "We make war that we may live\nin peace."\n
Who said it?\n
Aristotle.\n
You know your history.\n
I had a good teacher.\n
It has always been like this.\n
People making the same mistakes, over and over...\nand still all we can do is fight.\n
I hear ya. If you've got a goal, you've got to keep\nmoving forward.\n
I noticed you call Che Guevara "El Che."\n
Not just us. Everyone in these parts does.\n
Che was always his nickname. It does not feel\nright to call him by his last name.\n
...I was shocked the first time I saw you. You look\nso much like him.\n
I look like "El Che", huh?\n
Sort of. Not in the face. It's more... the way you\ncarry yourself...\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: I guess Che's a hero to the Sandinistas, too?\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Of course. The FSLN was formed in the spirit of\nthe ideologies championed by El Che and Fidel.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Fidel... Fidel Castro. So you're trying to bring the\nCuban Revolution to Nicaragua.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Well, we were. But Cuba isn't what it once was...\nNot since El Che left.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: El Che was a true revolutionary. He fought - and\ndied - for the people.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: He worked harder than anybody, and he was a\nrighteous man.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Even as a minister of Cuba, he gave up his\nweekends to work on the farms and public works.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: As a volunteer, no less.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Yeah, I've heard the stories.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: But when you think about it, wasn't it that\nobsession that did him in?\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: How do you mean?\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: We can't all be supermen. He thought the ideals he\napplied in Cuba would work in Bolivia.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: But, he failed to win converts and the support of\nthe peasants, and it cost him his life.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Maybe... maybe you're right.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: But at least he did not steal from those peasants,\nno matter how hard things got.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Yeah.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: I can sympathize with that.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: There's plenty of guerrillas out there who'd rob\ntheir own people to feed their revolutions.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: If we had a comandante like him, the Sandinistas\nwould find the will to fight.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: You called that giant chopper an "hombre nuevo"...\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Si. It means "new man."\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: New man?\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: There was nobody piloting that thing. It must be\ncontrolled by machine.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Yeah, it seems that way. No human being could pull\noff those crazy maneuvers.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: But it's not crazy - it's smart. It sings, too.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: When we first saw it, one of my men said, "Pilot\nmust be an hombre nuevo."\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Me, I do not like the name.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Why?\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Hombre nuevo was what El Che was striving to\nbecome.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: What all of us who joined the Sandinistas strive to\nbecome. That's why!\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: An hombre nuevo is one who finds joy in virtue\nand voluntary labor...\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: It makes me furious to see the name given to such\na monster.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: I'll bet.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Chico called that helicopter el colibri...\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Our name for the hummingbird. You saw how that\nchopper moved...\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: how it hovered in midair like a hummingbird.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Hell've a lot bigger than a bird, though.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: True. But better than hombre nuevo, don't you\nthink?\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: When you get kidnapped by el colibri, it's all over.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: They take you to a prison camp, and torture you\nuntil you snitch on your compas.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: That's what took Chico...\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: They have no mercy. Once you've talked, they toss\nyou out like trash...\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: I knew this, and still I could not save Chico.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: If he cannot be saved, I'll do what must be done...\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Don't write him off like that.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Sometimes you have to survive, even if it means\nsacrificing your honor.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: I'll get him back. I promise.\n
Snake, I need your opinion. How strong are the\nenemy's mercenaries?\n
They're well trained. They've got more than enough\nmen...\n
Seasoned, too - a lot of them probably saw action\nin Vietnam. They're a tough bunch.\n
And armed to the teeth.\n
I don't think I've ever seen a mercenary force field\nthat many tanks and attack choppers.\n
It shows how much cash they have to throw\naround.\n
And connections - how did they get access to\nsuch weapons?\n
How do you think? They're backed by the one and\nonly CIA.\n
And here we are, half of us farmers and the other\nhalf students. Children, even!\n
And weapons... We're so short on guns we have to\nsteal them from the enemy.\n
As much as I hate to say it, we're always going to\nbe on the defensive.\n
I know.\n
And mi viejo... Without him, we...\n
Yeah, I know.\n
...I don't know if we can win.\n
Can we, Snake?\n
Stop feeling sorry for yourself.\n
But...\n
Amanda!\n
What?\n
Listen to me. Don't ever let your men hear you talk\nlike that.\n
You're their leader, and a leader has to stand tall.\nEven when times get tough.\n
When it feels like the fear and uncertainty could\ncrush you.\n
You're the one your comrades look to for\nreassurance. That's what a leader is. Don't forget it.\n
...Snake...\n
If you're looking for comfort, go find a church.\nThat's all I've got to say.\n
You are right. I am sorry. I need to pull myself\ntogether.\n
You'll be fine. I know you have it in you.\n
Thank you, Snake.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Claymores are directional anti-personnel landmines.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Their blast radius is approximately 70 vara (60 yd),\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: sending over 700 metal fragments through the air\nat a 60º angle.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: But since they're directional, you can simply disarm\nthem from their blind side.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Get down low and approach the mine from behind,\nthen deactivate and recover it.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: To do this, press <I=ACT> when the Icon appears.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: You can use any unused Claymores you recover.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: You can also destroy them by shooting them.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Just keep your distance or you'll get hit by\nshrapnel. Best to use a sniper rifle.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: The only downside is you can forget about using\nthem yourself.\n
The land in our country belongs to us, and yet it\ndoesn't belong to us.\n
How so?\n
Along the coast, it is all banana groves. And in the\nmountains, it is coffee.\n
I guess in that way it's not so different from here.\n
Plantations...\n
Almost all the bananas and coffee are sold as\nexports.\n
The landlords keep the money for themselves,\nleaving precious little to the farmers.\n
Worse, the biggest landowners in the country are\nSomoza and his family.\n
But it does bring in foreign currency...\n
I doubt even that, at least for bananas. The\nplantations are owned by American corporations.\n

The bananas are processed in factories on the
plantations and exported to America from private
ports...
It's like having little American enclaves along the\ncoast of Nicaragua.\n
But the farmers have no choice but to go work\nthere...\n
Es ridículo! The people have to take their land\nback.\n
It is one of the things we're fighting for.\n
Tell me... when exactly did you realize your dad\nwas working with the KGB?\n
About six months ago. Up until then, we only had\nbeans to eat.\n
And then suddenly we started to get eggs and\nflour. Our bullet shortage simply disappeared.\n
How'd he get the cocaine?\n
Ask the KGB. All we did here was process it.\n
Coca plants grow here, too,\n
but to my knowledge almost all of the stuff we\nused came from Colombia and Bolivia.\n
It's processed in a factory and then shipped to\nports on the Caribbean Sea.\n
Where does it go after that?\n
I never thought about it.... I mean, I did not want to\nthink about it.\n
The biggest cocaine consumer in the world is the\nUnited States.\n
I'm guessing they smuggle it in on vessels\ndisguised as fishing boats.\n
Wait. La CIA uses that route, too.\n
Are you telling me they're selling cocaine to their\nown country?\n
Looks that way.\n
Those bastards are turning their own children into\njunkies? Are they insane?!\n
No, just afraid. Afraid of a communist Central\nAmerica.\n
La CIA calls their new toy Peace Walker, eh?\n
Yeah... So?\n
It is a insult to us Nicos.\n
Because of the guy you were talking about?\nWalker?\n
Si, although it happened over a hundred years ago.\n
Back then, the political parties in Nicaragua were\nat each other's throats.\n

The Nicaraguan Democratic Party hired an
American mercenary to help counter their enemies,
the Conservative Party.
And that was Walker.\n
After taking care of the Conservatives,\n
Walker decided to seize power in Nicaragua for\nhimself, eventually making himself president.\n
The Democratic Party gave him an inch, and he\ntook the whole country.\n
But it didn't end there.\n
Not only did he make English an official language,\nhe tried to reintroduce slavery.\n
Walker's goal was to build a "Caribbean Empire"\ncentered on the American South.\n
Caribbean Empire... hmh. Sounds kind of like what\nColdman is trying to pull off.\n
The gringos are always like that.\n
They invent some convenient excuse to trample all\nover foreign countries like they own the place.\n
Peace Walker... ha!\n
What happened to Walker in the end?\n
A united Central American army led by Costa Rica\n
kicked his ass and sent him running back to\nAmerica.\n
Then why don't we do the same? I for one don't\nintend to let Coldman get his way.\n
Good idea... I'm glad we have you, Boss.\n
Amanda! When did you join up with the Sandinistas?\n
About a year ago, when I went into the mountains\nwith mi viejo and his group.\n
I thought your dad was with the FSLN from the\nstart.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: No. He fought alongside General Sandino, but after\nthat he retired for a while.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: He found a job, got a wife and a house, and raised\nus kids.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Then one day some Sandinista students came by...\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: And he felt the old fire in his belly?\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Something like that. All he did was help them\nescape from la Guardia, though.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: But then la Guardia showed up.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: They broke into our house and began pushing him\naround, shouting questions.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: I'm guessing he kept his mouth shut.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: No matter how hard they hit him. Our house was\ntrashed.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: After that, he was on their list - they harassed him\nday and night.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: It was only then that he gave himself over to the\nSandinistas.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: He kept it hidden from us at first, so we would not\nget hurt.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: He sounds like a good father.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: He was... But my mother got fed up with it. She left\nus. I don't blame her.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Why didn't you go with her?\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: It was a hard decision, for sure.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: But like my father, I couldn't let Somoza get away\nwith his crimes. But most of all...\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Chico.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: ...He is too much like his papá. One way or the\nother he was going to stay.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: And I could not leave him behind.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Soon enough la Guardia drove us out, and we\nfound ourselves in the mountains...\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: It just kind of happened\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: For an accidental revolutionary, you sure put up a\nhell of a fight.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: The mountains make men into warriors. The\ntraining is harsh,\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: but it brings us that much closer to being hombres\nnuevos.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Chico couldn't ask for a better sister.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: I can see why they picked you to be comandante.\n
When I was little, I came down with malaria.\n
Unlucky for me, it was the bad kind. I was in a\ndaze the whole time,\n
and at one point they said I was not going to make\nit.\n
Malarial encephalopathy. I hear it's pretty common\nin tropical malaria cases.\n
Even today, my memory sometimes gets a little\nfuzzy.\n
Since then I've had this fear of mosquitoes... When\nI hear them buzzing nearby, I get jumpy.\n
That explains the chain-smoking?\n
Si. I thought it might help keep the mosquitoes\naway, just a little.\n
Maybe it's all in my head. You're the same way,\nright?\n
I will say this - I prefer a cigar over mosquitoes.\n
Me, too.\n
I've gotta hand it to you. It takes guts to conquer\nyour fear like that\n
and live a guerrilla's life in the wild.\n
It is nothing. El Che did not let asthma stop him\nfrom leading the revolution.\n
Compared to him, I am no hero.\n
I'm sorry to hear about your dad.\n
Thank you for saying that... Mi viejo was the leader\nof the frente.\n
He was the last of the generation that knew\nGeneral Sandino...\n
He saw the General's exploits first-hand as a boy.\n
He would tell us stories about it all the time... and\nabout how the General was assassinated.\n
Did you know he was getting money from the KGB?\n
I had some idea... But I did not have the courage to\nconfront him about it.\n
I know it was a painful decision for him to make.\n
I can imagine.\n
Yes, my father was a good man. I loved him as a\ndaughter. And his soldiers believed in him.\n
Thanks to him, la Frente held together even in the\nworst of times.\n
I don't know if I can ever fill his shoes...\n
Chico's 12, right?\n
Right.\n
Isn't he a little... short for his age?\n
...Malnourishment. Food is hard to come by when\nyou're running around in the jungle...\n
He's got quite an appetite.\n
I know!\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: I didn't want him to come in the first place.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: But there was no one to take him in. I had no\nchoice but to look after him.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Don't be so hard on yourself.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Sometimes it's better for a kid to be with his family\nthan far away, in a safe place.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Thank you...\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Promise me this, though. When your fight is over,\nmake sure he gets a proper education.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Give him a chance to be something other than a\nguerrilla.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: It's not too late to teach him something other than\nfighting.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: OK. I promise.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: ...You know what book Chico really likes?\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: The "World Encyclopedia of Mysterious Creatures."\nThe Loch Ness Monster, the Yeti...\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: UMAs. Yeah, I know.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: He's still so much like a boy... I worry about him.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: He'll be fine. I know plenty of grown men who still\ngo crazy over UMAs.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Are... are you serious?\n
You've taken such good care of me since you\nsaved me from el colibri.\n
I want to return the favor.\n
Just wait until you're healed up. Then we'll talk.\n
I appreciate that. But you need all the help you\ncan get.\n
It might take a while for me to heal completely,\n
but I'll be fine once I'm on my feet. Put me in a\ncombat unit - I'll pull my weight.\n
I wouldn't expect any less from a Sandinista\ncomandante.\n
Enough flattery.\n

But seriously, it does not feel right for me to be
sitting here while my compas are out risking their
lives.
One thing's for sure. Having you out in the field\nwould be a big boost to Sandinista morale.\n
Of course, our ultimate goal is still the overthrow\nof Somoza.\n
But until we get ourselves back in order, we will\nfollow your lead, wherever it takes us.\n
Glad to have you on board.\n
Amanda, you getting used to Mother Base?\n
Yes, it is Heaven compared to living in the\nmountains.\n
We're no longer constantly on the run from la\nGuardia or mercenaries.\n
Some of the new guys we've recruited used to be\nmercenaries...\n
We're getting along. It was difficult at first,\n
but once you talk to them you realize we've got\nplenty in common.\n
I see. Good to hear.\n
We may be enemies, but we're all still human\nbeings...\n
La CIA's soldiers, la Guardia... The same goes for\nthe people of America.\n
What's gotten into you?\n
Mi viejo got involved with drugs in order to scrape\ntogether money for la revolución.\n
He did whatever the KGB said.\n
All for Nicaragua... or so he told himself.\n
But I realize now... In the end all he did was help\npoison young people of America.\n
Yeah.\n
...I've made up my mind. Even when I leave Mother\nBase and return to la revolución,\n
I will never turn to drugs. Nor will I look to the KGB\nfor help.\n
If we topple Somoza using the KGB and drug\nmoney, we will lose the people's hearts.\n
So you're choosing a different path from your\nfather.\n
I still respect him. But I will not do things the way\nhe did.\n
Well, I'm sure Chico will be glad to hear that.\n
Chico is a grown soldier now. I could not face him\notherwise.\n
Well said, Amanda. Those are the words of a true\ncomandante.\n
Stop... I was inspired by the greatest comandante I\nhave ever known, Boss.\n
Amanda, how do I get to the prison camp?\n
First head up the narrow mountain path.\n
The path will gradually open up, and you'll come to\na fork in the road.\n
Watch yourself up there.\n
You'll be lower than the surrounding terrain,\n
so if you head down the middle you'll make for an\neasy target.\n
Thanks for the heads-up.\n
Take the leftward path to reach the prison camp.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: What can you tell me about the prison camp?\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Well, it used to be a village - until they took control\nof it.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: It is a maze of paths, so watch out for soldiers on\npatrol.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: I'll be sure not to stop and say "hi."\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Use the paths carefully and you should be able to\nstay out of view.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Where are they holding Chico?\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: One of the houses, most likely. You can peek\nthrough the doors.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Just press <I=ACT> when the Icon appears.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: You could also listen to any sounds inside for clues.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Good idea.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Guards will still be on the move while you're looking\ninside. Make sure you don't get caught.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: And Snake...\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: I know. I'll bring him back.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Thank you. I know I can count on you.\n
Amanda, do you know the way to the rail terminal?\n
Remember the locomotive? By the fork in the road\nbefore the village?\n
Yeah, back in the jungle.\n
Follow the train tracks from there and you'll come\nto the terminal.\n
But there's a plant along the way.\n
Disguised as a coffee factory?\n
...Yes, it is their drug refining plant. La CIA controls\nit now.\n
Cutting through there is the shortest way, but it'll\nbe crawling with soldiers.\n
If you want go around...\n
No, forget it. If that's the shortest way, that's the\nway I'll take.\n
Besides, it's one of their bases. It'll be good intel.\n
Very good. A number of the guards at the plant\nare positioned on high walkways.\n
Be sure to study their movements before you\nadvance.\n
Or I could just snipe them first...\n
The plant's layout is another maze, I'm afraid. Stay\ncool.\n
Make your way out of the plant and you'll arrive at\nthe terminal.\n
You know a lot about this place...\n
What are you saying? I've been there before -\nwhen the KGB ran it - yes,\n
but it is not as if I enjoyed it.\n
No, I just meant you know a lot about how the\nenemy works.\n
I hope so.\n
Anyway, did you talk to Chico about the terminal?\n
He said it's where they transfer the cargo onto\ntrucks.\n
Meaning the facility is of considerable importance\nto them. Don't get careless.\n
I won't.\n
By the way,\n
I've heard of a shortcut that cuts straight to the\ncoffee factory to the east of the village,\n
but I've never used it myself. Check it out if you're\ninterested.\n
Thanks for the tip.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: An enemy tank! Is there somewhere you can hide,\nBoss?\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: There are train cars, but they won't hold up\nagainst a gun like that.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Even a freight train? Incredible!\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: But they'd keep me out of sight - temporarily.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Use them to look for an opportunity to hit its\ntreads or the fuel tank at the back, but...\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Don't forget about that gun, huh?\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Or the soldiers. They may try to flank you.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Right.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: You can also stop it by taking out all the soldiers.\nYou can do it, Snake!\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Amanda, do I have to take the fork in the road\nback to the village?\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: People say there is a shortcut. Go back to the\ncoffee factory entrance,\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: then follow the path on the right.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: That will take you straight to the village.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: They may have increased security in that area,\nthough.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Not surprising, after what happened with the tank.\nWhat do I do once I'm back at the village?\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Destroy the barricade at the north side. From\nthere you can reconnect with the transport route.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Hmm... I'll need C4 for that.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: The explosion will bring everyone running too.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: There's probably going to be a fight - one way or\nthe other.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: They might not see you if you stick to the\nnarrower pathways.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Then just climb over any obstacles.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Don't let your guard down after taking out the\nbarricade, either.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Chico says there's a bridge north of the village.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Yes, a narrow one - for crossing the pipe.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: On the other side of that is the road the trucks\nuse,\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: though it's collapsed in places.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: I'll have nowhere to run if they spot me.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: They could be blocking the road, too.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Is there another way?\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: There is a path along the cliff.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: After you cross the bridge, there are ruins of a\nfort on the mountain.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Going through there would be a little easier.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Once you come to the end of the mountain path,\nyou'll be at the fort.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: That fort was built during the civil war. It seems la\nCIA's troops are occupying it, now.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: This just gets better and better.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: They've got gun turrets set up all around, from the\nlooks of it.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Attract too much attention and you'll really stir up\nthe hornet's nest.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Maybe I'll try and find a way around.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: You could always commandeer one of the turrets -\na little target practice, perhaps?\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Just like Krasnogorje.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Krasno-what?\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Sorry, just... thinking about old times.\n
Watch out! It's el galápago!\n
It reduces its body weight by blasting air\nunderneath it.\n
That makes it a lot faster than any tank. It also\nhas a tight turning radius.\n
Any weak points?\n
Taking out its boosters could reduce its\nacceleration...\n
You could also try destroying its machine guns.\n
I'll give it a shot.\n
We've lost many compas to that thing. Send it to\nthe scrapyard!\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: From here on in you'll be in a cloud forest. The\nground is covered in vegetation.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: You'll have plenty of hiding places, but so will the\nenemy.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: I'll keep an eye out for scouts.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Trying to force your way through would be suicide.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Know the enemy's location before making any\nmoves.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Too bad you don't have some sort of radar.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: I could try night vision.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Once you know where an enemy is, decide how you\nwant to handle him.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: You could get into his blindspots...\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Or drop him from a distance before he even has a\nclue someone's around.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: An eye for an eye, right?\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Don't even think about facing a chopper head-on.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Guerilla tactics would work well in a place like that.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Moving from tree to tree will make it hard to get a\nfix on you from the air.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: That's your best chance.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Good thinking, comandante. You clearly know your\nway around a battlefield.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Enough, Boss. Time to stop talking and start using\nyour ears.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: When you're hiding, you won't be able to see the\nchopper that well.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: It's important to use sound to get a read on its\nposition.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: You could also try taking out its tail rotor. That\nwould greatly reduce its mobility.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: And watch out for ground troops.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Copy that, comandante.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: The paths there are buried in vegetation.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Work with nature to conceal yourself, and you'll be\nmuch harder to spot.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: A ghillie suit would be perfect here.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: In any case, take caution when advancing. Don't\nwear anything that stands out.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: The ruins are a labyrinth, so try and keep your\nbearings.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: I can use those walls to stay out of sight.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Once a sniper is spotted, he'll move to another\nlocation.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: You shouldn't stick to the same place, either.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: I know. I learned all about that in the Soviet Union.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: It's not necessarily a good idea to try to engage a\nsniper in close-quarters combat.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Finally, once you've found a place to hide don't let\nthem take you from behind.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Don't worry. No one sneaks up on me.\n
Snake, be careful when going through areas you've\npassed through before.\n
The enemy could be waiting to ambush you.\n
And do you know how to identify the soldier with\nthe ID card?\n
Yeah, Cécile told me. He's in a forest with some\nquetzals, wearing an orange jacket.\n
He'll be from the lab. Probably out on patrol. Do a\nbody check to see if he's got the card.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: El colibri may be powerful, but he can be defeated.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Looks like you have a lot of places to hide there.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Remember your fight with the other chopper.\nGuerilla tactics will be key.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Only this one's got a few more aces up its sleeve.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Yes. It might try to crush you by taking out the\npillars.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Also, watch out for the smaller craft that abducted\nChico, the chicolibrí.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Chicolibrí...\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: It means "son of colibri." If it gets you, you'll just\nhave to wriggle your way out.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: You might get away if you're lucky.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: I'd rather not have to take that chance.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: Indeed, that would be best.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: I remember those barracks.\n

speaker: 0x0e3bb338
text: They're full of criss-crossing pathways so visibility\nis terrible.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Perfect for sneaking.\n

text: They've survived all this time - just undiscovered\nby man.\n

text: But they're finding fossils in America, too.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: This one they found three years ago in Texas had\na wingspan of more than 12 meters!\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: If I saw a gigantic pterosaur like that, I'd probably\ncall it a god, too.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: Yup, I'm sure that's what the quetzalcoatl really is.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: A base disguised as a mine? We never made it\nthat far.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: I don't know what kind of place it is, but you'd\nbetter be careful - just in case.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: I plan to.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: I've heard that the American army keeps dead alien\nbodies and UFOs in secret bases.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Aliens?\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: There are billions of stars in space.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: You've gotta think that at least a few have\ncivilizations more advanced than ours.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: I'll bet they visit Earth in UFOs.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: the army actually announced they'd caught a flying,\ndisc-shaped object near Roswell, New Mexico.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: Maybe you don't know about it, but those army\nguys, they all know!\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: You don't say...\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: Anyway, there's no telling what kind of mystery\nweapons they might have stashed up there.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: Watch your back.\n
Apparently, UFOs are connected to cattle\nmutilations.\n
Cattle mutations?\n
Not mutations. Mutilations... It's a word I'd never\nheard before.\n
People have been reporting their livestock dying\n
in mysterious ways near the same places where\nUFOs have been sighted.\n
They say\n
the bodies are drained of blood and the eyeballs\nand sexual organs are gouged out.\n
When you leave a corpse cut open in a field\nsomewhere, the ground soaks up the blood.\n
Yeah, but supposedly these cows weren't cut up\nby any man-made means.\n
Maybe maggots got to 'em?\n
In some cases they detected radiation.\n
Radiation...\n
Even in our own town we had goats that died in\nstrange ways.\n
Some said they saw a monster\n
- a lizard on two legs, covered in spines from its\nhead all the way down its back.\n
I wonder if that's what the aliens look like,\n
or if it was some pet they brought with them...\n
...Either way, it doesn't sound like a very advanced\ncivilization to me.\n
If you see one, tell it I said "hi!"\n
Sure... if it speaks human.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: UFOs kidnap people, too - you know, alien\nabductions.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: You've heard of the Hill Abduction, right? That\ncouple back in the 60s.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: So when I first saw the colibri, I thought it was a\nUFO.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Ah, the Fulton recovery.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: I know those guys are working with the aliens.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: Even if they wouldn't let me see them...\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Better not get caught again, or they'll be\nexperimenting on you!\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: I'd take that over torture...\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: What do you think they look like?\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: Completely bald, maybe, with gray skin and big\nblack eyes?\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: Or maybe they're four vara (11 ft) tall and wear\nskirts?\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: I kind of doubt it... I'll give you one thing, though,\nI've never seen anything move like that.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Maybe the CIA really did make contact...\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: You see?! It's true!\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: You wanna know something? I once met an alien\ncat.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: An alien... cat?\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: Yep. It was dark out so I couldn't see too well,\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: but it was a cat with a huge long tail.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: Its eyes shined in the dark, too.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Most cats' eyes do...\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: At first I thought it was a regular cat. But then it\nstarted talking to me - inside my head.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: ...Inside your head?\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: He said his name was Altargozo Elbakki Munyudar.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: He'd come to Earth from the Andromeda Galaxy to\ncheck out Earth's nuclear weapons...\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: The Andromeda Galaxy... Mankind's barely made it\nto the moon.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: We couldn't possibly launch nukes that far.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: Elbakki said he was watching over us - to make\nsure we don't destroy ourselves with nukes.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: Until the day we humans are ready to join the\nSpace Federation...\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: ...It's a shame. This is supposed to be the era of\nDétente,\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: and still we've got people pulling stunts like\nbringing nukes into peaceful countries.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: If something ever went wrong and set off a chain\nreaction of retaliation...\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: I know. This planet could destroy itself at anytime.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: Snake, is it true you took a picture of el colibri?\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Yep. Got it right here.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: Whoa! It's like an actual UFO! I knew it - los\nyanquis are working with the aliens!\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: I know it kind of looks that way, but...\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: Hey Snake, can you make me a copy of that?\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: I don't see why not. What for?\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: People pay good money for this stuff. We can use\nit to raise money for MSF.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Ha, sure, kid. You go out and get us a good price\nfor it.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: You don't believe me, do you? I'll get the money.\nYou'll see!\n
Snake, legend has it a place called Isla del\nMonstruo is near Costa Rica.\n
Isla del Monstruo?\n
It was discovered in the 18th century by\nCaribbean pirates sailing over to the Pacific.\n
And the island in "Treasure Island" - it's based on\none near Costa Rica, too.\n
Treasure Island? I remember reading that.\n
You've read it too? That makes things easier.\n
In Nicaragua we too have a story about a group of\npirates that encountered\n
a flying monster out at sea.\n
Some even say they landed on this monster island,\nthough we still don't know exactly where it is.\n
That's the reason I've always wanted to come to\nCosta Rica.\n
Ha, I see.\n
I heard another story... about a talking cat that\nlives somewhere in Costa Rica.\n
They say it'll take you to this place.\n
Interesting stuff.\n
Wanna know more about the island?\n
Maybe later. If I'm headed that way you can fill me\nin.\n
OK. Just lemme know!\n
Chico. I, uh... I met that talking cat.\n
The legendary Trenya? Really?!\n
Trenya? Yeah, that's what it called itself. Is it\nfamous?\n
In certain circles, yeah.\n
I'm still having trouble believing it.\n
I never thought I'd be talking to an animal one day.\nWhat a world.\n
Amazing you could understand its language.\n
Picking up the local lingo is one of the basics of\nintelligence work.\n
That's what makes you the Boss, Boss! Hey, say\nsomething in Trenya's language, will you?\n
Meow? Meow... Meow meow meow...\n
Wow! I have no idea what you're saying!\n
...Of course you wouldn't.\n
So what did Trenya say?\n
It said it would take me to that island you talked\nabout.\n
Really?! Take me too, Boss! Please, please!\n
I know you must be excited, but we don't know\nwhat's out there.\n
It could be dangerous. I'll scout it out first.\n
No fair!\n
Come on, Chico. This isn't as cut and dry as you\nthink.\n
You can come next time, depending on what I find.\n
I'll take some photos if I get the chance. Sorry,\nkid, but that's life.\n
Apparently there are other cats that talk besides\nTrenya on Isla del Monstruo.\n
There's more of them?\n
Yep. They're called the Felynes, but supposedly\nthey don't ever come to Costa Rica.\n
You should try talking to them if you spot them.\nWho knows what kinda stuff they have to say.\n
Yeah. Just when you think things can't get any\ncrazier...\n
Also, the Felynes are nice to humans, so you be\nsure and be nice back.\n
Don't you go attacking them or anything.\n
I would never hurt a defenseless little kitty.\n
I used to have this book full of pirate lore.\n
It had this story about Rathalos, King of the Skies.\n
Most accounts describe it as a dragon with wings,\nor a wyvern.\n
A wyvern... A two-legged dragon. Vlad the Impaler's\ncoat of arms had one on it.\n
Yeah, and he was the model for Count Dracula.\n
There are reports of ships being attacked out in\nthe middle of the ocean,\n
so Rathalos must be able to fly great distances.\n
And what's more, Rathalos is said to breathe fire!\n
Breathe fire? An animal like that can't possibly be\nreal!\n
We're talking about a monster, Snake. Forget what\nyou think you know!\n
Tigrex is a wyvern just like Rathalos.\n
But it's good at moving around on land, too.\n
It can blast you with rocks from a distance, or\nrush at you with incredible speed.\n
People have seen it on land?\n
Sí.\n
It's said that these two lady pirates, Anne and\nMary, visited Isla del Monstruo.\n
