It was there that they did battle with Tigrex.\n
Anne was quite a marksman, wasn't she?\n
Must've been a heck of a battle. I wish I'd been\nthere.\n
You know, I'm not so bad with guns myself...\n
I've already seen how good you are.\n
Anne and Mary also saw little dinosaurs running\naround the island.\n
Velocipreys?\n
Yup. As you'd expect they're very nimble - but no\nmatch for a firearm.\n
You wouldn't want to get surrounded by them,\nthough.\n
I'll bet. Nobody wants to be outnumbered in battle.\n
Right. Your best move would be to make sure they\ncannot encircle you.\n
Well, stealth is the basis of all solo sneaking\nmissions...\n
While it makes battle tougher,\n
working alone has its advantages when it comes to\ninfiltration.\n
That's what makes you the boss, Boss! You don't\nneed any advice from me.\n
Not bad for an old-timer, eh Chico?\n
Nope. Still, be careful.\n
Have you heard the legend about the dinosaur that\ncame back to life as a zombie\n
and attacked people?\n
Zombie?! You mean the living dead?\n
Yeah. Dinosaurs may be extinct,\n
but technically it would be possible for one to\ncome back to life as a zombie.\n
Not so fast. Dinosaurs were real, zombies... not so\nmuch.\n
What are you talking about, Boss!\n
Zombies have been used as slaves on Haitian\nplantations for years.\n
In Haiti they've handed down a secret zombie\npowder for generations.\n
...Really?\n
People from long ago must have used that same\nstuff on dinosaur remains.\n
But dinosaurs had been extinct for millions of\nyears before the first humans-\n
That hypothesis has to be wrong.\n
...In any case, this zombie was incredibly powerful.\n
Its name was Gear REX. They say nothing could kill\nit.\n
Some say its bodily fluids would burn right through\nyour flesh.\n
Then the spines that fell off its back would impale\nyou,\n
the pain made even worse by the deafening roar\nrattling every bone in your body.\n
...You sure it wasn't just some really strong\nmonster?\n
Who knows what kind of dinosaurs were out there.\n
We could be talking about something strong\nenough to resist small arms fire.\n
Are you afraid of zombies, Boss?\n
...No. I just find the whole thing hard to believe.\n
A fantasma is an espiritu that wanders this plane\ninstead of going to el Cielo.\n
There are different interpretations, of course, but\nthat's what I think.\n
See, the fantasma has a reason for remaining in\nthis world.\n
And if that were, say, a deep hatred for someone,\n
they just might be capable of inflicting harm on\nthat person.\n
You probably realize this, but your weapons or\nCQC won't work on fantasma.\n
And since they're not physical beings, they can\npass right through solid objects.\n
But, if you can eliminate their reason for remaining\nhere,\n
you should be able to help them reach el Cielo.\n
People say words can work wonders on fantasma.\n
You could try talking to them through CO-OPS\ncommunication.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: You can't always see fantasma with your naked eye.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: If some unseen presence is making a noise, you\ncan be sure one is around.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: When that happens, try taking photos in the area.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: You should be able to see what's causing it.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: Why do they show up on photos?\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: I'm not the one to ask about that, but...\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: Maybe fantasma are somehow able to deceive our\nminds - on a subconscious level.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: They're right there in front of us, but they whisper,\n"Hey, we're not really here!"\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: But a camera is a machine, so they can't do\nanything to it.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: Yeah, that's it! That's gotta be it!\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: That's a rangefinder camera you have, right, Snake?\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: Mi viejo used to talk about rangefinder cameras,\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: and how they can focus just as well as any other\ncamera, despite their size.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: He also said they don't have much picture blur,\neither.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: To bring an object into focus,\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: make sure the two images overlap before taking\nthe picture.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: But you could probably do that in your sleep,\ncouldn't you?\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: All you need to worry about is making sure your\nsubject is in the frame.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: Remember, Snake, photography is all about timing.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: Amanda is so bossy. It's always "Follow me" or\n"Stay here."\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: The other day she told me, "Chew your gallo pinto\nbefore you swallow."\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: Can you believe it?\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Knowing your sister? Yeah, I can.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: The enemy could strike at any time.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: I can't sit around taking my sweet time eating!\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: I'm a Sandinista just like the others.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: I don't need some woman telling me what to do!\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: ...Some woman? She's your sister,\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: and she's doing the best she can to fill your\nfather's shoes.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: I know, I know, but... lately, she hasn't been doing\nso good.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: I... Should be strong for her.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Now you're talking.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Sorry to hear about your dad.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: Don't be. He was... He is a guerrilla warrior.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: We pledge our lives to our country and its people...\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: I'm ready to die, too, if I have to.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: You sure?\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: You'd better believe it! Like mi viejo used to say,\n"Patria o Muerte."\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Che said it first.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: My dad used to tell us all kinds of stories.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: About General Sandino and his fight against la\nGuardia...\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: And about my mom before she left us.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: You didn't want to go with her?\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: It's not like that. La revolución comes first, that's all.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: You must wish you could see her, though.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: I dunno. But I know I'll see her again when this is\nall over. Somehow I just know it.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: When I do, me and mamá and papá are all going to\nlive together again.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: At least...\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: At least, that's what I thought.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Hang in there, Chico. Your sister needs you.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: OK.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: Have you ever heard, "Shoot, coward, you are only\ngoing to kill a man"?\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Che's last words.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: He'd been captured in Bolivia,\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: and said it to the soldiers just as they were about\nto execute him.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: El Che... He was something, wasn't he?\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: Coming up with a line like that knowing he was\nabout to die.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: After the Cuban Revolution,\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Che gave up his position in the new government to\naide in revolutions in other countries.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: He knew he could die at any time, and he was\nready for it.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: Me, I couldn't take even a little torture...\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: But you've been reborn, as an hombre nuevo.\nRight, Chico?\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: Right...\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Don't you ever get lonely living away from your\nmom?\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: Not really. My compas are my family now.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: A lot of them are from the same village as me.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: So you had plenty of people to take care of you.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: Take care of me?! I'm a warrior, like any other\nSandinista!\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: We look out for each other. That is how it works.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Sorry. Guess I misspoke.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: Now we're scattered because of that colibri... I\nwonder where everybody went.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: Hey, Snake. If you see any Frente prisoners, please\nyou gotta get them out, OK?\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: Those guys are solid - every one. You could use\nthem in MSF.\n
Hey Snake, are there any jobs for me here at\nMother Base? I can do anything!\n
You don't have to work, you know.\n
Don't treat me like a kid. I'm a man now.\n
OK, then, what are you good at?\n
Let me think... uhh... Everything! Put me on any\nteam. I can pull my own weight.\n
Ha... Well, you are young. You'll probably be a fast\nlearner. I'll think of something.\n
Anything you need, Boss! You'll see - I can fight as\ngood as anybody.\n
What's with all this sighing? You're not your usual\nself.\n
Oh. Snake.\n
Something on your mind?\n
Huh? No, not... really. Not really... I guess...\n
Hey, Snake...\n
Uh huh?\n
Girls are funny, y'know?\n
You can never tell what they're thinking, they're\nalways doing their own thing.\n
Maybe they really are different from us men...\n
Wh-what's this about now?\n
Chico... do you have a crush on somebody?\n
No! It's not that! I just...\n
What? Go ahead, you can talk to me.\n
...Whenever I talk to Paz,\n
my heart starts pounding and everything I say\ncomes out wrong.\n
Paz? I guess she is... pretty close to your age.\n
That ever happen to you, Snake?\n
Well, sure. It happens to everybody.\n
Well, how do I talk to her?\n
...That is a tough one.\n
Uh... Why don't you try... talking to her like you talk\nto everybody else?\n
No... It doesn't work. I freeze up every time I'm\naround her.\n
Our eyes meet, and my face starts burning for\nsome reason...\n
It's like living on the battlefield - you'll just have to\nget used to it... her.\n
You're nervous at first, but the more you're out\nthere, the more natural it feels.\n
Get your courage up and go talk to her more often.\n
OK.\n
Man, girls are more full of mysteries than UMAs...\n
You got that right.\n
Chico, I heard you saw Paz trying to sabotage\nZEKE before she activated it.\n
I should have stopped her...\n
If only I hadn't run away...\n
I could have captured her before she got inside...\n
If I'd done that, she'd still be here...\n
She was carrying a gun - probably trained to use\nit, too.\n
Don't blame yourself. You couldn't have stopped\nher anyway. You were unarmed.\n
I could at least have talked to her...\n
If I'd promised not to tell anyone, Paz wouldn't\nhave gone and done what she did...\n
It's just... It's just... I was so shocked, I panicked -\nran away...\n
Chico... when you saw Paz, she was trying to\nsabotage it, right?\n
Huh? Well, yeah...\n
And right after that, she took control of it - tried\nto make me surrender.\n
Something doesn't add up.\n
Why would she sabotage ZEKE when she was\nabout to use it against me?\n
Her actions were inconsistent, even for a spy.\n
If she wanted to destroy ZEKE, she could have\ndone it and run away.\n
But if her goal was to steal ZEKE, she'd have no\nmotive to sabotage it.\n
I don't know...\n
Maybe your seeing her caused her to change her\nplan? I don't get it...\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: ...You think Paz was planning to double-cross\nCipher?\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: Without ZEKE, she wouldn't have any way to\nthreaten you.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: If that were the case, she could have told me all\nthat from the beginning.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: She wouldn't have had to try and sabotage it.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: I guess so...\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: But that was the day before Peace Day. Paz was\ngoing to sing in a band. I couldn't wait to hear her.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text:
What if she wasn't going to double cross them...
maybe she just wanted to at least be able to enjoy
that...

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Chico...\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: I knew it... If only I hadn't run away...\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: If I'd talked to her... promised I wouldn't tell\nanybody...\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Don't second-guess yourself. Think about who\nmight have been hurt if you'd kept quiet.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: Yeah, but...\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Besides, we don't know for sure she's dead.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: She was ejected into the ocean. And she had\nscuba equipment with her.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: Yeah...\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Stop beating yourself up over the past, Chico - put\nyour hope in the future.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: The past is the past, but the future is up to you.\n

speaker: 0x0e559953
text: ...Right, Boss.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: AI stands for artificial intelligence.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: It refers to a manmade machine possessing an\nintellect on par\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: with that of a human being.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Is that even possible?\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: Possible? You've seen it with your own eyes.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: What the AI weapons are capable of.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: How Peace Walker carried out The Boss' will in the\nend.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: No mere machine could ever choose to sacrifice\nitself like that.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: I just can't see how a bunch of circuits and\nswitches could have a will of its own...\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: It's called The Ghost in the Machine, Snake... And it\nexists.\n
Let's say, hypothetically, there really was an\nintelligent machine.\n
How would you prove it?\n
What's the difference between a high-level\ncomputer and an AI?\n
It depends on what you choose to define as\nintelligence...\n
For example, Snake, listen to my voice talking to\nyou now. Suppose it were an AI?\n
Say what?\n
What if the living, breathing me, sitting here\ndrinking tea and talking to you,\n
were actually an AI, programmed to simulate my\nthoughts and my voice?\n
You're nuts.\n
No, I'm not. You couldn't prove I was a real human\nbeing, could you?\n
It'd be... No.\n
Hm. So if an AI is so advanced you can't tell it\nfrom the real thing,\n
wouldn't you call that intelligence?\n
I'm not quite convinced.\n
But that's only one way to look at it.\n
It's roughly how Dr. Turing explained artificial\nintelligence.\n
The test I described is called the Turing Test in his\nhonor.\n
Yeah, well, it sounds like a bad joke to me.\n
That singing monster of yours put me through hell.\n
If I never meet one again, it'll be too soon.\n
Shame. And I was about to let an AI take my place\nin our conversation.\n
Don't even think about it.\n
Dr. Alan Turing is known as the father of computer\nscience.\n
It was he who formulated the basic theory of AI.\n
During the war, he worked for GC&CS.\n
The government's cryptology school... the one that\nbroke Enigma.\n
The very same.\n
Without him, they might never have been able to\ndecipher the Germans' code.\n
...But then they arrested him.\n
Why? Weren't his some of the greatest\ncontributions to winning the war?\n
Homosexuality was a crime in Britain back then.\nAnd he was gay.\n
I know exactly how crushed he was. I feel it's my\nduty to further his AI research...\n
Like "The Imitation Game," huh?\n
Ah, you know it, then?\n
The clue that inspired the Turing Test came from\na trifling little party game.\n
You exchange written notes with another person\nbehind a screen,\n
and try to guess their gender whether they're a\nwoman,\n
or a man pretending to be a woman....\n
It's surprisingly difficult to tell the difference. Man\nor woman, human or machine...\n
What do the differences even mean?\n
Dr. Turing was fascinated by the differences\nbetween men and women.\n
Perhaps that's what led him to formulate his test.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: What if you hadn't used The Boss as the model for\nthe AI?\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: What do you mean?\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: If the end goal is MAD, seems like there are more\nsuitable models out there.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: A military chief of staff, or a nuclear technician...\neven the President.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: Patriotism, leadership, good judgment...\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: Each of those qualities is essential when deciding\nwhether to launch a nuke, and she had them all.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Wouldn't the President, too?\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: It's not enough. She had the will for it.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Will?\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: Let me explain, Snake. Peace Walker is a\nstand-alone weapon.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: It has to decide on its own whether or not to\nlaunch a nuke.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: It can't turn to anyone else for advice.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: It can't do its job if it's not prepared to take sole\nresponsibility for the fate of the world.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: I know of no other human being who could bear\nthat burden.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: ...That's it?\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: There were technical considerations, of course. To\nbegin with, the female brain\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: is a more appropriate model for an AI.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Wait...the female brain?\n
What do you mean by that... modeling your AI after\nthe female brain?\n
Snake, what is the human mind capable of that a\ncomputer is not?\n
Being... lazy?\n
Interesting response. And not incorrect...\nBut the answer I was looking for was empathy.\n
Empathy?\n
The ability to feel for others, to be more precise.\n
Love for a child, pity for the weak, grief for the\ndead.\n
All of these are particularly well developed in the\nfemale brain.\n
That's stretching it a little.\n
On the contrary, it's perfectly reasonable.\n
The male brain, on the other hand, may be well\nsuited for systematic thinking,\n
but it's less able to empathize. In that sense, it's\ncloser to a computer.\n
So, if your objective is to make the AI think more\nlike a human...\n
You need to teach it to how to empathize like a\nwoman?\n
The novel "Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?"\ndeals with this very problem.\n
In the book, an empathy test is used to distinguish\nbetween machines and human beings.\n
As machines become more and more advanced,\n
our society will gradually become more and more\nsystematic.\n
Our cities will teem with robot-like people unable to\nfeel for others...\n
We cannot allow that to happen.\n
Computers must learn to empathize. The same\ngoes for humans, only more so.\n
Well...What about yourself? You make these claims,\nand yet\n
I've never seen you empathize with a real person.\n
It's true. Until now, I was a prisoner of death.\n
It was my intention to die upon the completion of\nMammal's development.\n
She was my one reason to live.\n
But you changed your mind?\n
...I did. Because she taught me the dignity of living.\n
My eyes are open now. I want to go on living, and\nseeing real people.\n
I see.\n
Is it really necessary to make machines think like\nhumans?\n
I'd think empathy would get in the way of making\nthe decision to retaliate.\n
I admit, human thought may not be fully compatible\nwith level-headed decision making.\n
Then again, is there such a thing as non-human\nthought?\n
The moment computers became so advanced\n
that they could calculate faster than human\nbeings, a new dream was born.\n
Dream?\n
If we can create a machine that can do advanced\nmathematics,\n
why can't we create one that can think like a\nhuman?\n
The 19th century author Auguste Villiers\nl'Isle-Adam wrote a book called "Tomorrow's Eve"\n
in which the protagonist fashions an artificial\nwoman to serve as his ideal lover...\n
I believe the idea of creating an intelligent being\nwith our own hands\n
is one of mankind's oldest dreams.\n
So AI is a product of people's dreams then.\n
Not only AI. Civilization itself\n
is the process by which mankind gives form to its\ndreams.\n
But not all dreams are pleasant.\n
Some have expressed fears about "non-human\nintelligence."\n
Yeah, they want the benefits with none of the risks.\n
Some fear that intelligent robots might rise up and\nrebel against their human masters,\n
as portrayed by the Czech writer Karel Capek in\nhis "Rossum's Universal Robots."\n
Or in the 1970 film "Colossus: The Forbin Project,"\n
where intelligent supercomputers in the U.S.\n
and the Soviet Union join forces and plot to\nsubjugate humanity.\n
Isaac Asimov offered a specific solution to these\nfears with his Three Laws of Robotics,\n
which demonstrated that while robot intelligence is\ndifferent from that of humans,\n
the two can coexist.\n
In order to endow computers with intelligence,\n
we must first have a thorough understanding of\nwhat intelligence is.\n
And that is where the need for a practical and\nfeasible expert system arises.\n
So what's an 'expert system?'\n
The AI housed within Peace Walker began\ndevelopment as such a system.\n
An expert system is a type of proxy program\n
by which a computer makes decisions as an expert\nwould.\n
The program "MYCIN," for example,\n
is a system that decides which kinds of antibiotics\nto prescribe.\n
The system asks the patient a series of questions\n
to narrow down the range of appropriate drugs.\n
So you programmed Peace Walker to prescribe live\nnuclear warheads instead of penicillin.\n
What I realized, however, was that a simple expert\nsystem wasn't up to the task.\n
You need more than expertise to launch a nuke.\n
Indeed. Expertise is a necessary prerequisite but\ninsufficient on its own.\n
Deciding to launch a retaliatory strike requires\nconsideration of a wider range of factors.\n
In such a scenario, the entire global situation\nbecomes the criterion for making a decision.\n
Makes sense. You screw up the prescription, and\nthe whole world goes into anaphylactic shock.\n
A "weak AI"\n
that has only a limited range of knowledge upon\nwhich to base its decisions won't cut it.\n
Therefore, I had the AI study The Boss' thought\npatterns,\n
thus creating a true expert system - a "strong AI."\n
You couldn't leave the world in the hands of\nsomething\n
with anything less than an absolute worldview.\n
I could have built a simple expert system in no\ntime at all.\n
Say, how would you like a system that decides\nwhich guns you should equip\n
according to the mission's parameters?\n
I'll pass. I'm not gonna leave my life up to\nsomebody else's judgment.\n
Especially not a machine.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: With current technology, AI are inevitably enormous\nin size.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: But as circuit integration continues to advance,\nthey'll become even smaller.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: As small as human brains, and perhaps smaller\nthan that.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: And in the meantime robotics will continue to\nadvance as well,\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: to the point where we can create androids, robots\nthat resemble humans. And then...\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: And then what?\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: Well, I don't need to spell it out for you, do I?\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Don't tell me you're thinking of making an android\nimitation of The Boss...\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: Surely the thought has crossed your mind as well?\nOf one day being reunited with her?\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Enough! I don't want any part of it!\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: ...I see. I didn't mean to offend you.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: In reality, AI is more likely to evolve in the opposite\ndirection anyway.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: The opposite direction... What does that mean?\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: More and more AI are becoming systems that\nspecialize in mass information processing\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: - without human intelligence, thought, or emotion.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: A machine that has no individualism or sense of\nself,\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: but rather behaves as a collective, exhibiting the\nqualities of a society.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Like a beehive?\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: Yes. It aggregates data collected by individuals and\ndetermines how the collective will act\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: just as honeybees travel between the hive and\nflowers.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: The key to achieving that will be networking AI\ntogether.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: I don't know how to say this, but... that kind of\ngives me the creeps.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: But if your goal is to control society, it's the better\nmodel to use.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: It lets you filter data - disseminate only what you\nwant disseminated.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: Of course, I myself have no interest in an AI\nwithout a shred of life to it.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Earlier, you called the Mammal Pod a butterfly. Not\na pupa or a cocoon, but an imago.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: Yes. The AI that came before the Mammal Pod\nwere works in progress.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Works in progress?\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: They were enough to keep the frame running.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: But not enough to make decisions about nuclear\nretaliation.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: They weren't quite complete. They were pupae.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: Only when I added The Boss' data did the AI take\non its true form,\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: becoming a butterfly and taking flight.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: And that's why the nose art on Peace Walker was\na butterfly...\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: I gave the Mammal AI the code name "BS-Imago."\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: BS is short for Boss.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Huey called that gigantic unmanned chopper a\nChrysalis.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Is that another one of your AI code names?\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: Yes. You're referring to the TJ-Chrysalis 6000.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: There's also the GW-Pupa 5000, the TR-Cocoon\n7000...\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: I get it. A hovercraft type and a treaded type....\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: And those letters on the front, TJ and GW or\nwhatever, those are initials?\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: Correct. The initials of the American Presidents\nwhose faces are carved\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: into Mount Rushmore.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Then you're missing one.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: I assigned that one to the Reptile Pod. AL-Aurelia\n8000.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Aurelia... another word for chrysalis... a pupa just\nbefore it emerges.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: All of the initials except for "BS" were of Coldman's\nchoosing.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: I chose mine from the storied ranks of British\nroyalty.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: MS, AV, EW...\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: ...What do those stand for.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: You can't guess? Why, Mary Stuart, Alexandrina\nVictoria, and Elizabeth Windsor...\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: ...All queens. Of course.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: What did you mean by "the Ghost in the Machine"?\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: Oh, that... It's a term coined by the philosopher\nGilbert Ryle.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: You've heard of Descartes, yes?\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: I think, therefore I am...\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: That is the one. Descartes espoused the dualistic\ntheory of mind and body.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: He believed that our thinking minds exist in a\nseparate dimension from our bodies,\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: which are governed by the laws of physics.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: But if that were true, then couldn't you say that a\nmechanical "body"\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: inhabited by a ghost "mind" is a human being?\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: Ryle criticized Descartes on those grounds,\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: saying such a thing surely wouldn't be human.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Why'd you bring it up?\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: I wasn't thinking of Ryle in particular when I said it.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: I simply thought that if a person is composed of a\nmachine and a ghost,\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: perhaps the opposite is true as well.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: Perhaps by placing a ghost inside a machine, we\ncould in effect give birth to a new person.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: And that was your idea for the Boss AI?\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: The moment you ripped the memory board out, the\nMammal Pod ceased to function.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: It should have been dead.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: And yet Peace Walker righted itself, singing a song\nof peace.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: I couldn't help but feel... that her soul had come to\ninhabit Peace Walker.\n
Are you familiar with the film "2001: A Space\nOdyssey"?\n
I've heard of it, but...\n
Of course not. I didn't expect you to be cultured\nenough to appreciate such things.\n
Yeah, thanks. Anyway...\n
2001 features an AI called HAL,\n
a highly advanced system that controls an\nexploration spacecraft.\n
It can converse with people, and even play chess.\n
Huh. Now where have I heard that before...\n
The way HAL was portrayed was truly superb.\n
How so?\n
HAL is given secret orders that not even the\nship's captain knows about.\n
Naturally, he's not allowed to divulge them to the\ncrew. The stress of it causes HAL to crack.\n
Crack?\n
Go crazy. Though there are those who interpret it\ndifferently.\n
One by one, HAL kills off the crew until the captain\nfinally shuts it down...\n

The film offers amazing insights into AI - their
growth, their utility, their faults - and their fear of
death.
You must have found it useful in your research,\nthen.\n
Must you always be so... utilitarian?\n
It doesn't matter whether or not it's useful. What\nmatters is that it inspired me.\n
Then it was USEFUL.\n
Never mind. The portrayal of HAL wasn't the only\nwonderful thing about the film.\n
It was full of hints about the future of human\nevolution. Truly a film for the ages.\n
Strangelove, when did you and The Boss first\nmeet?\n
...Did she ever tell you about what she saw in\nspace?\n
Yeah.\n
I saw the same thing along with her.\n
The Soviets beat America into space with Sputnik,\n
and so America rushed to be first in manned\nspaceflight.\n

NASA used her as their top-secret guinea pig,
launching her deep into the cold blackness of
space.
I took part in the project. As a scientist.\n
You were there with her...?\n
Yes... For a brief time, we were one and the same,\nshe and I.\n
We sought each other out... Completed each other.\n
Did you know that inside every woman there's a\nuniverse,\n
and that we are able to sense this in each other.\n
We connected because of our empathetic female\nbrains.\n
As time went on... I began to have doubts about\noffering such a noble soul as sacrifice.\n
Why would they...? Why did she have to...?\n
...The flight test was a narrow success, and she\nmiraculously made it back alive.\n
But her mind and body were horribly mangled, and\nthere was nothing I could do for her.\n
We were no longer one and the same.\n
She went away, and I, having nothing else to live\nfor, immersed myself in AI research.\n
Hoping that no one would ever have to make her\nsacrifice again.\n
I never knew...\n
It's not really worth knowing.\n
We were ships passing in the night, that's all.\n
Perhaps someday I'll tell you the long version, if\nyou're interested.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: That was quite a warm welcome you gave me at\nthe base in Costa Rica.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: ...Sorry about that. But I simply had to know.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: The Boss' final act?\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: Yes. By inputting her thoughts and actions into the\nAI, I was imbuing it with her mind.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: The only thing I couldn't understand was her final\nact.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Operation Snake Eater...\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: Official history says she betrayed her homeland\nand defected to the enemy... and was killed by you.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: ...But it didn't make sense. The Boss would be the\nlast person on earth to betray her country.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: It was logically inconsistent.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: ...It was, wasn't it?\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: That internal inconsistency prevented the AI from\nactivating properly -\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: just as HAL malfunctioned in the film.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: I understood the reasoning. But I had to have\nproof.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: Proof of her final act. Her true intentions. One way\nor another!\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: So you tried to squeeze it out of me, huh?\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: As a matter of fact, I did. Your silence was the\nvery answer I was looking for.\n
That white horse The Boss rode....\n
The Andalusian, yes.\n
How'd it get to Costa Rica?\n
I went looking for it. It was her final witness, even\nif it couldn't speak. I found it and brought it here.\n
Where? I thought for sure it'd be blown to ashes\nby those MiGs...\n
I searched the ends of the earth for that horse...\n
and found it at last in a horse market in Britain.\n
Britain? Are you saying it came all the way over\nthe Ural Mountains,\n
through Europe, and across the English Channel?\n
Who knows, really? Perhaps someone took it there.\n
Wait, the thought never occurred to you it might\nbe a different Andalusian that only looks the same?\n
I can't prove it... Or rather, I couldn't.\n
What do you mean?\n
You should know best of all. That horse wouldn't\nlet anyone ride it.\n
And believe me, I nearly killed myself trying.\n
The only one it allowed on its back was you...\n
That was the proof, though I hate to admit it.\n
...And to think I ran it to its death.\n
But in that last run, it regained the glory of its\nyouth.\n
Using the last of its strength to pursue its former\nmaster...\n
Any horse would wish for such a fine end.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: What did you think of Peace Walker's final act?\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: I recreated her thought patterns exactly.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: It was exactly what she would have done.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: The world's most empathetic mind weighed the\npast, the future,\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: and the entire world... and decided not to retaliate.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: Merely knowing that is enough for me.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: ...So what you're saying is, we don't need\ndeterrence to have peace?\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: I didn't say that. What's important is that we wish\nfor peace.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: MSF needs a way to protect itself from the might\nof nations.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: Survival requires pragmatic thought and action.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: But, you still must retain your ideals.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: If the gap between reality and those ideals ever\nleads you to lose them...\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: I doubt MSF will survive.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Strangelove... Is that a code name?\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: No, just a nickname.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text:
Don't tell me you don't recognize it! From Kubrick's
"Dr. Strangelove, or How I Learned to Stop
Worrying and Love the Bomb?"

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: It's a film that came out in 1964... a dark comedy\nabout the absurdity of nuclear deterrence.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: You were in a movie?\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: No, stupid! I got my nickname because of that\nmovie.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Why, because you look like the doctor in the movie?\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: ...No. That Dr. Strangelove was a man.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: So...\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: Back when I was at ARPA (Advanced Research\nProjects Agency),\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: I kept a photo of The Boss on my desk.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: I was totally engrossed in my research and showed\nno interest in the opposite sex,\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: plus I had a photo of a woman on my desk...\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: The fools around me turned it into a cruel taunt,\ncalling me "Strangelove."\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text:
Even for a bunch of shut-ins who never went out
to the cinema, that title seemed to ring true with
them.

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: Anyhow, in their eyes homosexuality was something\nstrange.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: They were incapable of seeing things outside the\nlens of their own standards.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: Being strange means you have your own unique\npoint of view. I rather considered it an honor.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: So you were with ARPA before you came here,\nhuh?\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: Yes. Back then it was really the only place I could\nmake a living from my AI research.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: And before that?\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: I started out at NASA. That's where I met her.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: When Boss went into space...\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: ...Yes. It was that incident that turned me away\nfrom aerospace engineering.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: Space is entirely too hazardous a place for human\nbeings.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: That was why I felt an immediate need to develop\nAI.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: As it turned out, rockets later became much safer,\nand mankind reached the surface of the moon...\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: In any event, it was a hollow Cold War victory.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: When you get down to it, a nuclear missile is just a\nrocket with a nuclear warhead strapped to it.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: Thus, taking the initiative in the space race was\ntantamount to a military show of force.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: But the budgetary strain was too big for\nWashington or Moscow to handle.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: Yes, and then there was the Cuban Missile Crisis\nand the Vietnam War. And then came Détente...\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text:
Having leapt ahead of the Soviet Union with its
moon landing, America shut down the Apollo
program in '72.

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: It was around then that ARPA was downsized and\nrenamed DARPA, the "D" standing for "defense."\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: With few prospects for continuing my AI research,\nColdman's invitation was a godsend.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: It was also a chance to have them collect data on\nher.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: The end result being this mess.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: But we did learn something valuable from her - the\nnobility of peace.\n
Why'd you agree to come here - to Mother Base?\n
You intrigued me.\n
Me? ...Hold on, you're not planning on modeling\nyour next AI after me...\n
Not a bad idea. But I have no intention of ever\nagain attempting to transplant\n
human thought into machines.\n
...That's a relief.\n
You are the man who inherited The Boss's will.\n
You're gathering people around you even now,\n
shaping them, building a new organization. I'd like\nto see how it turns out.\n
You're not planning to go back to AI research?\n
I never said such a thing. Of course my work will\ncontinue...\n
Here?\n
In my eyes, the growth of MSF\n
as an organization is analogous to the development\nof the nervous system.\n
The way you become intertwined, stimulate each\nother,\n
branch out in new directions... It's really quite\ninspirational.\n
Interesting way to put it.\n
Of course, I intend to repay you for your\nhospitality.\n
The fruits of my research will be at your disposal.\n
Why not assign me to the R&D team? I promise you\nwon't be disappointed.\n
You know, that ID card I got from Huey wouldn't\nlet me into the lab.\n
Of course not. I deactivated it.\n
Why?\n
As though I'd let him into my lab!\n
You don't seem to care for him much. Even though\nyou two are in the same field.\n
Oh, please. For starters, I can't stand that\nwishy-washy attitude of his.\n
If he's got something to say to me, he should be a\nman and come say it in person,\n
not write some furtive letter.\n
But if his card doesn't work, how's he supposed to...\n
And another thing! The way he always demeans\nhimself.\n
Every other sentence begins with "I could be\nwrong, but..."\n
Why can't he just do what he does and be\nconfident about it?!\n
Well, there was the thing about his dissertation\nbeing plagiarized...\n
The real problem is, he doesn't have a whit of\nindependence in him.\n
In Costa Rica, and even back at NASA he was\nalways following people around\n
asking if there was some way he could help.\n
Why doesn't he stop his whining, take a stand, and\nface up to me?\n
I think I know how he feels....\n
And to top it all off, he seems to enjoy referring to\nhimself by that nickname I gave him.\n
I simply don't get it. How can he be so submissive?\n
So Huey was a nickname you gave him...\n
That's right. I took it from the name of a drone in\nthe science fiction film "Silent Running."\n
Drone?\n
It's a type of worker robot.\n
The way he follows people, just waiting for them to\nboss him around, is so similar. I couldn't help myself.\n
Oh.. It's an American film directed by Douglas\nTrumbull,\n
the man who did the special effects for "2001: A\nSpace Odyssey."\n
Imagine that. A scientist who likes science fiction...\n
And that's not all!\n
There's more?\n
He's a man!\n
...Hang on, I seem to remember you saying he\nshould be more of a man.\n
...Yes, well, he is an awfully good scientist.\n
Without his Reptile Pod, my Mammal Pod wouldn't\nfunction.\n
Just as the cerebrum can't exist without the\ncerebellum and the brain stem.\n
He did a fine job of designing it, I'll give him that.\n
That sounded suspiciously like praise...\n
Hmph. It's merely an objective observation.\n
I like people who possess the will to move forward.\n
I have no time for those who refuse to take\ncontrol of their lives.\n
Until he does, my opinion remains the same.\n
So...you and Cécile seemed to be enjoying\nyourselves back at that lab.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: What are you insinuating? I only kept her because\nI didn't want our secret to be known...\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: And the personal baths?\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: You could have left her in there alone and locked\nthe door from the outside.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: Yes, that, well... she seemed anxious, so I....\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Now why would she be anxious?\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: She was beautiful. I was only admiring her beauty.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: She was terrified.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: I never meant her any harm. She knew that. I know\nshe did.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: But she felt like she was in enough danger to run\naway.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: No matter what I did, if Coldman found her she\nwould have been...\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: You're right. The truth is I wanted to save her.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: But not if it meant forestalling the completion of\nMammal.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: So you made it easy for her to escape?\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: Do you really think I am that soft?\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: ...I'll admit, security wasn't exactly tight.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: It wouldn't have been difficult for her to escape\nfrom the building.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Seemed like she had a rougher time after she got\nout.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: At any rate, I never did anything to her to deserve\nany blame. Is that clear?\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: OK...OK, I believe you.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: Huey's probably mentioned this, but just to be clear,\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: there's a limit to the parts we can produce here at\nMother Base.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: Therefore, I've built ZEKE's AI using memory boards\nyou pulled from other AI weapons.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Will that work?\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: In the human brain, individual functions are spread\nacross multiple regions.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: The same is true of AI. Multiple parts sharing the\nsame function interlink to strengthen that function.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: For example, the more sensor memory boards you\nhave,\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: the greater ZEKE's search-and-detect capabilities\nwill be.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: Install more movement boards and you'll increase\nits mobility.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Meaning the AI's capabilities change depending on\nhow much memory we give it?\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: Exactly. The more boards you install, the more\npowerful a function will be.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: How's the ZEKE AI different from Peace Walker's?\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: ZEKE's AI isn't a replica of the human thought\nprocess.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: It isn't programmed to make decisions about\nnuclear retaliation.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: On the other hand, it is capable of highly\nindependent action in combat\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: when given orders from a pilot.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: It can protect infantry, destroy the enemy, and, if\nordered...\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Launch a nuke.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: Let us hope it never comes to that.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: My sentiments exactly.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: I'd better fill you in on ZEKE's speech synthesis\nsystem.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Speech synthesis system?\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: Humans speak for the conventional weapons they\nwield,\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: but an autonomous AI weapon is a different story.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: If the AI can't communicate with surrounding\nforces, how can they function as a unit?\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: True. Verbal communication is critical on the\nbattlefield.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: Thus, an AI weapon requires a dedicated system to\nproduce speech.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: To be precise, though, only Peace Walker was\ncapable of self-generated speech.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: All the other AI simply repeat preset messages\ndepending on the situation.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: ZEKE is no different. However, you do have the\nability to set those messages as you please.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: To create a message, go to the Extras Menu, and\nthen select Edit Mode.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: You thought of everything.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: You can even have it sing, too.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Sing?\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: Song can be a very valuable asset. I realized that\nat the lake.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: Naturally, ZEKE's AI doesn't allow for it to perform\noriginal compositions.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: It can only play back recordings provided to it.\n

speaker: 0x0ebd8542
text: I doubt you're much of a composer, Snake, but you\ncould always have a go at the lyrics.\n
That was some escape you made from\nStrangelove's lab.\n
Security inside was not so tight.\n
The door to my room was locked from the outside,\nof course.\n
But she took off the blindfold at bath time - so she\ncould wash my hair...\n
Pretty luxurious treatment for a prisoner.\n
Wasn't it? She wouldn't undo the handcuffs, but\nshe washed my body for me instead.\n
And with such gentle care...\n
Why'd you run away? Didn't she say you could go\nhome in a month?\n
If your escape attempt failed, you'd be in greater\ndanger than before.\n
I was supposed to be giving a presentation\n
on the distribution of Costa Rican bird species at a\nconference.\n
The date was approaching quickly.\n
So I pretended I had to use the toilet and made\nmy escape.\n
I found an ID card and searched everywhere for\nmy equipment and my tape...\n
But a soldier saw me. It was a miracle I managed\nto get away.\n
There was no time to find the tape.\n
I don't care about the conference. I'm lucky\nenough to still be in one piece.\n
You bounce back quick.\n
You don't?\n
....Not sure. I try not to dwell too much on the past,\nbut...\n
Then don't. There's no point. I'm so glad to be out\nof there.\n
I never felt safe, you know?\n
Tell me about it.\n
Well... I think she's interested in women. And I think\nshe took a fancy to me.\n
That's, uh.... huh.\n
Besides, it's much nicer here.\n
Was it just the two women in the lab?\n
Most of the time, oui.\n
Hmm...\n
And one of them, you only heard her voice, right?\n
Yes, that is correct. Such a wonderful voice. It\nsent chills up my spine.\n
What was the other woman like?\n
Don't even think about it. She's not the slightest\ninterest in men.\n
No, it's part of my mission to...\n
Only teasing. Let me think...\n
I believe she was in her 30s.\n
Pretty, with a good sense of style, but austere in\nher tastes.\n
A very... Unusual woman.\n
And she was doing research on AI?\n
AI? So that is what she was up to.\n
You know, she did say something interesting:\n
that people should not be going into space. That it\nis too dangerous.\n
Hmm, an automated control system for rockets,\nthen?\n
She said something about wanting to "get closer to\nher dying wish."\n
I think she must have been talking about an old\nlover.\n
Lover... You mean another woman?\n
My, aren't we curious about women and other\nwomen!\n
You want to hear the terrible things she tried to\ndo to me?\n
That's not what I meant...\n
It's all right, you can be honest.\n
...You two seemed to get along awfully well\ntogether.\n
No, no, not at all.\n
I think you're hiding something.\n
Never mind! Aren't you supposed to be looking for\nthe quetzal?\n
Here, I'll demonstrate its call for you.\n
I KNEW it...\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Let's go over this one more time.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: First, I need an ID card to get into the lab.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: That is correct. From the outside it looks like any\nother ruin.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: But on the inside it is a state-of-the-art research\nfacility.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: And your ID card got taken away from you by\nsome guy in an orange jacket.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Exactly. I heard a quetzal singing nearby.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: It has not been that long since it happened.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: It could be tricky if he's out on patrol, but if he's a\nstationary sentry...\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: You don't think the quetzal's moved?\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Its nest is probably nearby. I do not think it will go\naway anytime soon.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Good. I'll get on looking for that soldier.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: If you forget what it sounds like, I'll do the call for\nyou again.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Just give me a call anytime you'd like to hear it.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: I'll do that.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Let me get this straight. You were in Costa Rica\nas a birdwatcher?\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Yes, I was. Not for pleasure, though - I am a\nresearcher, after all.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: I am studying the distribution of Latin American\nbird species.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: With today's compact cassette tape recorders,\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: even a woman like me can carry her recording\nequipment by herself.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: But it was a mistake to come alone.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Mmm. Even so, there sure are a lot of wild birds in\nCosta Rica.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Aren't there? Over 800 different species,\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: said to be more than 10% of all living bird species\non Earth.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: How many can you name, Mr. Ornithologist?\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Hey, I was just trying not to scare you...\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: You should at least have a basic knowledge of\nCosta Rica.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: How about this: I will give you a thorough\neducation,\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Mr. First-Time Ornithologist.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Uh, OK. Start by telling me about the quetzal.\n
Cécile, what's that machine you said you use to\nmake those recordings of yours?\n
A cassette... something or other.\n
A cassette recorder? Or a cassette densuke, as\nthey say in Japon.\n
Yeah, that. What is that thing, anyway?\n
A portable recording device released last year by a\nJapanese company: Sony.\n
It uses compact cassettes, making it far lighter\nthan open reel machines.\n
It still weighs 5 kilograms, but the exercise won't\nkill me!\n
Ha.\n
It's user-friendly, too.\n
All the buttons have markings on them,\n
allowing you to operate it without looking at it.\n
Can you imagine missing the shot of a lifetime\nsimply because you'd blinked?\n
That would be devastating.\n
But where'd they come up with densuke? It sounds\nlike a Japanese name.\n
Allow me to field that one.\n
Kaz?!\n
Densuke's a nickname that comes from the name\nof an old manga character.\n
Was he some recording nerd, too?\n
Don't gimme that! Recording atmospheric noises is\nan exhilarating art!\n
There's nothing like capturing the real world in\naction on tape!\n
It's just like taking pictures with a camera,\n
only with a microphone instead of a viewfinder.\n
Sure...\n
Listen to a tape with your eyes closed\n
and the scene just bursts to life in your mind's eye.\n
Tell him, Cécile.\n
Absolutely. When I listen to the sounds of birds in\nmy apartment,\n
it's like I'm back in the forest where I recorded\nthem.\n
See, she's a Parisienne. She knows what's chic.\n
If you say so...\n
What do you like to record, Monsieur Miller?\n
Me? Steam locomotives, no question.\n
The roar of the engine, the throaty steam whistle...\nMore animal than machine.\n
Mmh, don't get me started!\n
Steam locomotives are a dying breed in Japan.\n
I wouldn't mind going back for a bit and making\nsome new tapes while I still can.\n
...You're less civilized than I thought.\n
L-LESS civilized?!\n
I detest those beasts. The noise frightens off all\nthe birds.\n
Then there's the smoke...\n
I much prefer the peace and quiet of the forest.\n
Cécile, wait! That... That came out wrong, I...\n
Sure it did.\n
Alright, what do you want to know about quetzals?\n
Hmm... Give me the basics, something that'll help\nme find one.\n
OK, then. First of all, as I'm sure you remember,\n
the quetzal's wings and back are emerald green\n
- a dazzling blend of viridian fading into blue.\n
Its belly is brilliant red, and its tail feathers are\nwhite. Such a gorgeous bird...\n
Also, the male has two long decorative feathers,\nbut only during breeding season.\n
Among birds, males are usually more beautiful than\nfemales.\n
Like a peacock's tail.\n
Yes, just like that.\n
It is interesting to note that while their bodies are\nonly 40 cm long,\n
many quetzals reach over a meter in length when\nyou include their decorative plumage.\n
Quetzals typically build their nests by making holes\nin dead trees with their beaks,\n
about three to four meters above the ground.\n
They're omnivorous and eat everything from nuts\nto lizards.\n
Where can I find one?\n
Their habitat stretches across the entire tropical\ncloud forest.\n
You may end up having to rely on its song to find\none.\n
Good to know...\n
I will do an imitation. Listen closely!\n
Kyohhh, kyohhh...\n
Not bad.\n
Shall I do a chicken next?\nCluck-cluck-cluck-cluck-bacaaak!\n
No thanks. That's enough.\n
Are you sure? How about a monkey?\n
...Don't need that, either.\n
Oh. All right, then.\n
You said you could do a monkey call.\n
Yes! Want to hear it?\n
Yeah, I won't be able to get it off my mind until I do.\n
Alright. Here it is, then.\n
...That's pretty good.\n
I can do others, too. Like a sheep, a pig...\n
Yeah?\n
Wow. What about a pig?\n
That's uncanny!\n
Ha ha. I can do a rabbit as well.\n
A rabbit? Rabbits make noises?\n
Certainly. But they're very faint,\n
so perhaps only someone who has owned one\nwould recognize them.\n
I see. So what do they sound like?\n
Listen very carefully.\n
OK.\n
Seriously? Rabbits sound like that?\n
I assure you, they do. Listen again.\n
Never heard a rabbit do that before.\n
They do, I swear!\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Costa Rica is the home to many hummingbirds as\nwell.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: The people here call them colibri.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Colibri, huh...\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Hummingbirds are the world's smallest birds.\nAlthough they can vary from species to species,\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: most are around 10 cm in length, and the smallest\nno more than five.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: It's amazing to think that something so small can\nstill be a fully developed bird.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: I'd think a bird that tiny would get mistaken for a\nbug.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Actually they are often mistaken for sphinx moths.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: The little darlings feed on flower nectar,\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: and their beaks are long and thin to help them\ndrink up the nectar.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: They beat their wings far faster than any other\nbird.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: The smallest ones over 70 times a second! Can\nyou imagine?\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: What for?\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: They hover in midair while they suck their nectar.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: They can even fly straight backwards.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Hovering... like a helicopter!\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: That's why Amanda and her unit called that\nchopper colibri.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: I think it is an insult to the birds to give their\nnames to weapons, don't you?\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Don't ask me. Ask the birds how they feel about it.\n
Have you heard of the manakins?\n
Never.\n
Unbelievable! You came all the way to Costa Rica\n
and you've never even heard of them!?\n
I didn't come here to look at...\n
Manakins are known for their beautiful courtship\ndances.\n
The Orange-collared Manakin is said to live on the\nPacific side,\n
the White-bearded Manakin on the Caribbean side,\n
and the Long-tailed Manakin is in the central basin.\n
The Long-tailed Manakins are especially distinctive.\n
What's special about them?\n
First, each young male picks an older male to\nteach him how to dance.\n
Then teachers and pupils all get in a group and\ndance for the females.\n
However, only the teachers get paired off with\nfemales.\n
The pupils practice their technique for seven years\nbefore striking out on their own\n
and finding their own pupils.\n
I guess it takes time to get good at anything,\nwhether it's dancing or soldiering.\n
Manakins always have plenty to eat.\n
Apparently that is why they have so much free\ntime to practice dancing.\n
Unlike us, obviously...\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Another well-known bird of the cloud forest is the\nThree-wattled Bellbird.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Wattled? What the hell's a wattle?\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: It is just like your beard, Snake!\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: What?\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: It's a piece of flesh that hangs down from its chin.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Kind of like whiskers, but not made of hair.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: A hanging piece of flesh?\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Oui, and it only grows on males.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Nothing more important to a man than his beard.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: So these birds are in the cloud forest, too?\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: They're normally found in the lowland rain forests,\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: but they migrate into the highland cloud forests\nduring breeding season.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: What the Three-wattled Bellbird's best known for,\nthough, is its loud call.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: It makes these metallic BONG! and DING! sounds -\nhence the name "bellbird."\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: It hardly sounds like a bird at all.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Even an expert bird caller like me cannot do it\njustice.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Doesn't sound like I'll be mistaking it for a quetzal.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Do you know the national bird of Costa Rica?\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Honestly! And you call yourself an ornithologist?\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: The national bird of Costa Rica is the Clay-colored\nRobin.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: It's a plain-looking brown bird found throughout the\ncountry.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Why'd they make it the national bird, then?\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Aren't there all kinds of better-looking birds, like\nthe quetzal?\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: The Clay-colored Robin has a most exquisite song.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: And I think it is part of the Costa Rican national\ncharacter\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: to choose a bird everyone knows and loves over\nprettier ones.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Somehow these people don't strike me as being\nvery "Latin."\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Speaking as an ornithologist, I am rather happy\nwith their choice.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Not all birds have to be pretty.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Oh, and just so you know, the quetzal is the\nnational bird of Guatemala.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: The Scarlet Macaw and the Great Green Macaw\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: are also representative birds of Costa Rica.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Macaws are a type of parrot... enormous, stately\nbirds.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Macaw... I think I've heard that name somewhere\nbefore.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: But of course you have - you're an ornithologist,\nno?\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Stop it....\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: So tell me, where do macaws live in Costa Rica\ntoday?\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Oh c'mon now...\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: I am only teasing you.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Macaws live not in the cloud forests,\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: but in the rain forests on the Pacific side of Costa\nRica.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: In the past, they were a common sight all across\nthe country,\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: but lately the population has decreased\ndramatically.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: One possible cause is the pesticides sprayed to\nfacilitate large-scale banana cultivation.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Evicted from their own land, huh.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Thankfully, conservation efforts have been gaining\nsome momentum lately.\n
Never heard the name "Cosima" before.\n
The again I don't know many people from France.\nIs it a common name?\n
No. Not that common.\n
But Wagner's second wife was named Cosima\nFrancesca Gaetana Wagner.\n
Huh.\n
You know, "Kojima" is a common last name in Japan.\n
Kaz?!\n
It's just funny how, you know,\n
I'm part Japanese and Cécile's middle name is so\nclose to "Kojima."\n
It feels like... destiny unfolding.\n
You think so?\n
Oui oui! That's a beautiful name you have. Cécile\nCosima Caminades.\n
Wait a second...\n
Cécile Cosima Caminades... Cosima Caminades...\nHey, that’s close to...\n
Close to what?\n
Your name... It sounds almost like the sentence\n“Kojima, kaminandesu” in Japanese.\n
And what does it mean, s’il vous plait?\n
Well, "kami" is the word for "god" in Japanese.\n
Nandesu... Well, it's hard to explain, but placed\nafter "god" it would turn the sentence into "is God."\n
Okay. So?!\n
Kojima is God... Cecile's name is a message!\n
I don’t believe it... Kojima is God... Kojima is God...\n
Umm, Kaz...?\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: How are you enjoying Mother Base so far?\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: It is wonderful!\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Good to hear.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: I was worried someone as cultured as you would\nfind the plant a little uncouth.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Uncouth?! You've got albatross, and frigatebirds,\nand terns, and tropicbirds...\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Seabirds I'd never have a chance to see in France!\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: ...Oh, well, great.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Sorry, I know I should not spend all day chasing\nbirds...\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: is there anything I can help with?\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Appreciate the offer. But I'm not sure what I could\nask you to do...\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Well, I'm certainly not cut out to shoot a gun...\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Cécile, where'd you learn to move through the\nforest like that?\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: The birds weren't scared of you at all.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Becoming one with the forest is the very essence\nof birdwatching\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: they won't behave naturally if they sense a human\nnearby.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: And that can really affect your observations.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: I see... Kind of like scouting, then.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: I am also good at spotting birds from a distance,\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: tracking them based on the tiniest of clues,\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: and being aware of my surroundings.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: You're starting to sound even more like a scout.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: The only way to find a bird is to think like a bird.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Now, think you can find a place for me?\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Yeah.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Did you live in Paris your whole life before coming\nhere?\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Yes. It is my favorite city.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Paris is the world capital of art and culture.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: It has the latest fashion, the best cuisine, and the\nmost elegant, refined people.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: The beauty of the Champs-Élysées at night is\nalmost unearthly.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: The name comes from Elysium, the name of\nParadise in Greek mythology.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Heaven, in other words.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Must be nice for some people. Not for me.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Are you saying the cultured life does not appeal to\nyou?\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: I'm saying I never had a chance to lead one. Not\nthat it appealed to me anyway.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: You prefer war?\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: I don't... Like war. Life outside heaven just suits me\nbetter.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: That is a hard way to live...\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: ...But if you do ever come to France, I will show\nyou around Paris.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Then you will see what heaven on earth is really\nlike.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Heaven on earth, huh... The only image I have of\nFrance is the Foreign Legion.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Th-that is how you view France?!\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: What do the French think of the them?\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: It is a difficult question... We normally don't think\nabout it so much.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Critics claim it forces foreigners to take on the\nmost dangerous missions\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: so French citizens won't get hurt.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: You're right, that probably had something to do\nwith why it was created...\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: But I understand that along with service comes\nbenefits\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: such as French citizenship and permanent\nresidency.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Those who join are all given an equal chance,\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: regardless of race, religion, education, social\nstatus, or national origin.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: So it can be a godsend for people from poor\ncountries.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: A way for the have-nots to live a decent life...\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: I guess that's not so different from MSF.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: There's one other image I have of France: the\nnational anthem.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Ah, La Marseillaise... Not everyone is a fan, of\ncourse.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: The whole "To arms, citizens. May an impure blood\nwater our furrows." thing, eh?\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: The song was composed right after the French\nRevolution.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Fearing what the tide of the Revolution\nrepresented,\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: the ruling classes in neighboring countries applied\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: all kinds of pressure on the young government.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: La Marseillaise became the anthem of the\nvolunteer armies that sought to protect\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: constitutional rule against that pressure.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: And they couldn't do that without armed force.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Oui. I agree, some parts are a little belligerent,\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: but we must not forget that if it were not for\nthem,\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: France would not be the democracy it is today.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Have you ever seen "The Umbrellas of Cherbourg"?\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: A movie? No, never seen it.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: No? It came out 10 years ago.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Catherine Deneuve, she is so beautiful in it.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: And the music, the costumes, the colors... Oh!\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: It takes place in the naval port of Cherbourg.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: That was a beachhead in Normandy.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: It is set back when young men were conscripted to\nfight in the Algerian War.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: The French government called the conflict a\n"public order operation in northern Africa."\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: I was still a little girl then,\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: but I can clearly remember one of my friends' older\nbrothers going off to fight.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Yeah, national service is required in France.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: The war splits up two young lovers.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Director Jacque Demy's lyrics and Michel Legrand's\nmusic tore at my heart.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: I will never forget its wonderful melodies. Aaahh...\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: You okay?\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: It changes lives - changes fates. War is not a good\nthing.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: For some reason it strikes a chord to hear that\ncoming from someone like you.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Speaking of the Algerian War of Independence,\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: you ever hear of "The Day of the Jackal"?\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: You mean the novel that was made into a movie\nlast year?\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: The OAS, a militant French underground group,\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: plots to assassinate De Gaulle, hiring a hitman\nknown as the Jackal.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Readers know that de Gaulle was not killed, but it\nis still so exciting.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: If someone was going to try to eliminate me,\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: I would hope they'd be as thorough as the Jackal.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: To know everything about me without me\nsuspecting a thing.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Oh, Yeah?\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: I wonder if my birds feel the same way.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: I wonder.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: France conducted its first successful nuclear test\nin the Algerian Sahara in 1960.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: A lot of French scientists took part in the\nManhattan Project.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: They defected to America to escape wartime\noccupation.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Correct. And once the war was over,\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: they returned to France and continued their own\natomic research.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: President de Gaulle did not want to have to rely\non an American nuclear umbrella for protection.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Thus making France the world's fourth nuclear\npower.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Some say the test's success pacified the Algerian\nrebels.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: The civil war was undoubtedly held in check.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: But never have I equated nuclear weapons with\npeace.\n
France has produced many philosophers over the\nyears.\n
Descartes, Bataille, Sartre, Baudrillard...\n
I'm familiar with Sartre myself.\n
He called Che Guevara the most complete man of\nthe century, didn't he?\n
Smart guy.\n
He does tend to sympathize with the left. What\nelse do you know about him.\n
...That's it.\n
You know nothing else?\n
...Nope.\n
Ooh la la. The man is one of the giants of\nexistentialism, you know.\n
Exitentialism? I've been meaning to look into that.\n
Nothing more dangerous than sneaking in without\nfirst securing an exit...\n
No, existentialism. Sometimes I wonder if my\nEnglish is not better than yours.\n
Sorry, I'm just... not into philosophy.\n
Is that so? I would imagine it might really enrich\nyour life.\n
I'd rather take action now than spend time thinking\nabout\n
what we are or how we're supposed to live.\n
I guess you could say I live my philosophy.\n
Interesting. That sounds like something Sartre\nwould say.\n
Yeah?\n
He says we're born with no defined nature,\n
and that we're free to make our "self" what we wish.\n
Free? So he was one of those devil-may-care kind\nof guys, huh?\n
No, actually he meant that because we are free to\ncreate our own life,\n
we must take full responsibility for our actions.\n
Man is condemned to be free, is how he put it.\n
Condemned to be free...\n
But then others will take it upon themselves to\ndefine who you are.\n
I've been feeling that way lately.\n
I keep telling people to call me "Snake," but nobody\nseems to listen.\n
Sartre also says, "Hell is other people."\n
Hell... Well we are outside of Heaven.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Do you have an interest in the visual arts, Snake?\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Not really. Please, no deep conversation...\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: But you have heard of Picasso, yes?\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Yeah, I've heard the name.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Sadly, Monsieur Picasso, co-founder of cubism,\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: passed away in the south of France last year.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: France was his home, you know.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Huh? I thought he was born in Spain...\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Do you know his full name?\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Pablo Picasso. Anyone would know he's Spanish\nwith a name like...\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Hmph. Shows what you know.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: What do you mean?\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: OK, here we go.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Pablo Diego José Francisco de Paula Juan\nNepomuceno María de los Remedios...\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: ...Cipriano de la Santísima Trinidad Ruiz y Picasso.\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: What do you think? That was his full name.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Still, I don't see how...\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: A master of modern art. A genius who crafted over\n100,000 works in various styles,\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: spending the greater part of his life in France. The\nman is a part of our culture.\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Yeah that kind of stuff is of limited use in my field...\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: But back to the point - Picasso was Spanish,\nright? Or am I missing something?\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: He wasn't French, right? Right?\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: Cécile?\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: What difference does it make?\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: It doesn't matter if he was from Spain or from\nMars,\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Picasso is Picasso. It does not change the fact\nthat he lived in France,\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: nor does it take away from his monumental legacy!\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Why do you care so much about where he was\nfrom, anyway?\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: Whatever happened to the "Sans Frontières" part\nof "Militaires Sans Frontières"?\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: You started it. "France was his..."\n

speaker: 0x0ec8dda0
text: What was that?\n

speaker: 0x0e28dce6
text: ...Nothing.\n
Tell me, Snake, do you ever put sweets in your\nrations?\n
Never thought about it before. Why?\n
I simply love them! French sweets are très délicieux.\n
Everyone knows crêpes, but there are also\nprofiteroles,\n
éclairs, madeleines, financiers...\n
Then there's Tarte Tatins, and you can't forget\nsavarins.\n
Oh, and mille-feuilles, crêpes, blancmanges...\n
You already mentioned crêpes.\n
Soufflés, croquembouches, canelés, floretins, kouign\namanns, Peach Melbas...\n
Finished?\n
...And macarons! I love those the most.\n
Macarons parisiens are the best.They're so cute\nand colorful,\n
and they contain meringue, so they melt right in\nyour mouth.\n
Wow. I'd no idea macaroons were that popular in\nFrance, too.\n
What do you mean "in France, too"?\n
Macaroons are those coconut-flavored cookies,\nright?\n
Excuse you! Macarons contains almond powder, not\ncoconuts!\n
Don't they have peanuts in them? I've had them in\nJapan a few times.\n
I thought they were called "makorons."\n
Makarons? Some cheap imitation, I am sure.\n
French macarons have a long and distinguished\nhistory.\n
They date back to the 16th century, when\nCatherine de' Medici of Florence\n
married into the French royal family.\n
The story goes that her pâtissiers shared the\nrecipe after they arrived.\n
That's a history of over 500 years.\n
So... they're originally from Italy, then.\n
Well...\n
Don't macaroons come from Italy, too?\n
Look, I do not really think...\n
Keep in mind "macaron" is almost identical to\n"macaroni."\n
Well, that settles it.\n
...I cannot believe this. To associate macarons with\nmacaroni!\n
You, Monsieur Miller, are an insensible oaf!\n
Hey, hey, why am I the bad guy? Come on, Cécile,\nwait! Cécile!\n
Hello! Snake, mon chéri.\n
You been drinking, Cécile?\n
Can't you please do something about this pest?\n
Who?\n
Monsieur Miller.\n
What's he done now...\n
Wine.\n
Wine?\n
He said he thought the soldiers might tire of\nhaving beer all the time,\n
so he's brought in some wine instead. And then he\ngave me a bunch.\n
That was... nice of him.\n
But the past two years have been bad for French\nwine.\n
Perhaps it is the bad weather we have had, but\nwhatever the case,\n
I told him the last thing you want to be drinking\nright now is French wine.\n
California and Chile have good wine, too.\n
But then he goes and stocks the pantry with\nnothing but French wine from '72.\n
The stuff is a disaster.\n
Then he says, "Come on, Cécile, have a taste of\nthe old country."\n
I had a terrible feeling about it, so I decided to just\ntaste it at first.\n
And then again, and then a few more times.\n
Took one for the team, huh?\n
But when you do a tasting, don't you usually spit\nthe wine out?\n
But bottle after bottle, nothing but garbage,\nabsolute garbage.\n
Not one half-decent bottle in the whole lot! "Taste\nof the old country" he says...\n
Sorry to hear that.\n
I cannot believe this! What will we do with all this\nwine!\n
The guys aren't too picky when it comes to taste.\n
You sound just like Monsieur Miller.\n
Huh?\n
When I complained, he simply said, "As long as it\ngets the job done."\n
You people are such culinary savages!\n
Allez tous vous faire voir ! ...Aaaah, somebody take\nme back to Paris! Please!\n
...I think you've had a little too much, Cécile.\n
You seem like a very... how do I put this...\nuninhibited woman.\n
You think so? I am no different from other Parisian\nwomen. Not since May 1968.\n
May 1968... The general strike that almost brought\ndown the president?\n
Right. But it was more than just a strike.\n
It started with the student movement at\nStrasbourg University in '66.\n
They did not want anything from the country, but\ninstead sought reform at the school.\n
That helped ignite a fire in the hearts of scores of\ndissatisfied young people,\n
and the movement spread all over France.\n
It was more than just opposition to Vietnam and\nthe de Gaulle administration\n
